claim: Imágenes en este video son del "Huracan helen en la Florida".
explanation: La creadora de la campaña de donaciones también publicó el video en YouTube, el 14 de agosto con el subtítulo: "Tormenta en Orem encontró su camino dentro del sótano de Redd". El artículo dice que el video es de la casa de una familia en Orem, Utah, que sufrió inundaciones severas luego de que el agua entró por la ventana de su sótano. Sin embargo, el segundo clip en el video en Instagram, de una cascada de agua entrando por una ventana cerca de un escritorio, no es del huracán Helene.

claim: "Profesores de la Universidad de Howard confirman: 'Kamala fue la peor estudiante de la historia'".
explanation: Una búsqueda inversa de imágenes muestra que el hombre de la publicación en Facebook es Bradford Grant, profesor de arquitectura de la Universidad de Howard. Hace más de 30 años que la vicepresidenta Kamala Harris se graduó de la Universidad de Howard de Washington, D.C., y una escuela de leyes de California. Harris también se graduó en 1989 de la Facultad de Derecho de la Universidad de California Hastings, ahora conocida como Facultad de Derecho de la Universidad de California, San Francisco o UC Law SF.

claim: Vice President Kamala Harris “was born in Canada.”
explanation: (Screengrab from Threads) Harris was born Oct. 20, 1964, in Oakland, California. RELATED: Kamala Harris is again facing attacks on her racial identity. A July 31 Threads post claimed Harris was not American because she "was born in Canada."

claim: The U.S. government is offering Americans loans to pay for flights out of Lebanon while they have been flying Israeli citizens out of Israel on chartered flights for a year “on our dime.”
explanation: We rate the claim that the U.S. government is offering Americans loans to pay for flights out of Lebanon while they have been flying Israeli citizens out of Israel on chartered flights for a year "on our dime" False. After Israel launched a military ground invasion in southern Lebanon on Sept. 30, the U.S. embassy in Lebanon said in a security alert Oct. 3 that the Beirut-based embassy can provide U.S. citizens with emergency loans to relocate and direct Americans to flights with available seats to depart to a safe country. About 1,500 Americans evacuated Israel on chartered flights in 2023 after Hamas attacked Israel on Oct. 7.

claim: A biolab caught fire in Georgia right before the 2024 election.
explanation: A Sept. 29 Instagram post sharing video of the fire was captioned, "A Biolab has caught on fire in Georgia." Today, the U.S. does not develop or produce any bioweapons as part of the United Nations’ Biological Weapons Convention. The Department of State said on X in 2022 that the U.S. is in compliance with the Biological Weapons Convention and "does not develop or possess chemical and biological weapons anywhere."

claim: Beyoncé and Taylor Swift announced a “big endorsement concert” and said, “No more silence, before it’s too late, our voice must be heard now!”
explanation: But neither Swift nor Beyoncé had formally endorsed any candidate of Aug. 27. Swift and Beyoncé endorsed Joe Biden and Harris in 2020. "Beyoncé and Taylor Swift are about to have a BIG Endorsement Concert," an Aug. 21 Facebook post said.

claim: “Country Music Television (CMT) has announced a permanent boycott of Taylor Swift.”
explanation: "In a move that shocked the country music community and beyond, Country Music Television (CMT) has announced a permanent boycott of Taylor Swift," a Sept. 16 Facebook post said. Singer-songwriter Taylor Swift hasn’t been banned from Country Music Television despite an old satirical post that’s regaining traction online. This Facebook post isn’t.

claim: Haitian immigrants are eating pets and wildlife in Springfield, Ohio.
explanation: Social media posts claim that pets and wildlife in Springfield, Ohio, are being eaten by Haitian immigrants. A Springfield spokesperson said the city has received no such reports, and Springfield police told a local news outlet the department has received no reports of pets being stolen and eaten. But are the social media claims true about the immigrants eating their neighbors’ pets and dining on local waterfowl?

claim: "Kamala just launched her presidential campaign on RuPaul's Drag Race."
explanation: Vice President Kamala Harris launched her presidential campaign soon after President Joe Biden announced July 21 that he would withdraw from the race and endorse Harris’ candidacy. On July 26, Harris appeared on the Season 9 finale of "RuPaul’s Drag Race All Stars," a reality competition show airing on MTV. And on July 23, Harris appeared before a crowd of thousands in Milwaukee.

claim: Kamala Harris “wants to forcibly compel doctors and nurses against their will to give chemical castration drugs to young children.”
explanation: During Harris’ vice presidency, the Department of Health and Human Services passed a rule that included LGBTQ+ people in the Affordable Care Act’s prohibition on sex discrimination. The change meant that LGBTQ+ people are again included in the Affordable Care Act’s prohibition on sex discrimination. An RNC spokesperson provided information about the Biden-Harris administration’s general support for access to gender affirming care for youth, but did not specify what Trump was referring to or a policy that would "force" doctors to provide care.

claim: California law lets you “rob a store as long as it’s not more than $950” and “not get charged.” Kamala Harris “did that.”
explanation: There is a $950 threshold cited in Proposition 47 between a misdemeanor or felony theft charge in the state. Trump said Harris was responsible for a California law that lets people steal with no penalties as long as the goods are valued at $950 or less. Under state law before Proposition 47, shoplifting property worth $950 or less was often a misdemeanor, but such crimes could, in some cases, also be charged as a burglary, which could be a felony, Harris’ summary said.

claim: Photo shows “domestic Antifa are already gathering in Chicago, to create chaos during the Harris-Walz DNC.”
explanation: And Chicago police have not said antifa is gathering in Chicago in such large numbers. When we contacted the Chicago Police Department about the X post’s claim, the agency pointed us to an Aug. 13 press conference about police efforts for the DNC. But we found no evidence from police or in on-the-scene news reports that demonstrators linked to antifa played a dominant role.

claim: Vice President Kamala Harris’ “60 Minutes” interview may be “a major Campaign Finance Violation.”
explanation: Trump said on Truth Social that Harris’ "60 minutes" interview might be "a major Campaign Finance Violation." And the answer to that question is, ‘Yes.’" And here’s the exchange on the same topic that was included in the full interview: Whitaker: "We supply Israel with billions of dollars in military aid, and yet Prime Minister Netanyahu seems to be charting his own course. A CBS News spokesperson told The Associated Press that Harris said both of the statements seen in the preview clip and the full interview back-to-back during her sit-down with "60 Minutes."

claim: FEMA, FAA are “blocking” delivery of Starlink devices and supplies to North Carolina’s hurricane-hit areas.
explanation: ET Oct. 4, Musk posted that a SpaceX engineer in North Carolina told him FEMA was "actively blocking citizens who try to help" Hurricane Helene survivors. Rumor" webpage, on which it addressed what it described as a "rumors," including that 1) the FAA was "restricting access to the airspace for Helene rescue and recovery operations" and 2) FEMA was "operating and controlling airports in western North Carolina." After entrepreneur Elon Musk claimed on X that FEMA was blocking relief efforts in North Carolina, social media posts multiplied, amplifying the claim and garnering thousands of views and shares.

claim: A Haitian woman was arrested in Springfield, Ohio, for eating a cat.
explanation: We rate the claim that a Haitian woman was arrested in Springfield, Ohio, for eating a cat Pants on Fire! Alexis Ferrell of Canton, Ohio, was arrested Aug. 26 on animal cruelty and disorderly conduct charges after Canton police said she tortured, killed and ate a cat in front of people in Canton. Now some social media users are sharing police footage of a woman being arrested for animal cruelty as proof that Trump was right and the fact-checkers are wrong.

claim: Sam Brown “said abortion should be banned without any exceptions for rape or incest.”
explanation: A Rosen campaign ad said Brown "said abortion should be banned without exceptions for rape or incest." Sam Brown said in the interview that he supported exceptions to abortion bans for rape, incest and when the mother’s life is threatened. A Dec. 5, 2023, Nevada Independent article reported that Brown’s campaign said it "disavows" and had "no involvement" with the 2022 questionnaire in which Brown said he supports abortion law exceptions when the mother’s life is at risk.

claim: Says his Jan. 6, 2021, speech on the White House Ellipse drew the “same number of people,” as the 1963 March on Washington where Martin Luther King Jr. gave his “I Have a Dream” speech.
explanation: (AP)   The question that triggered Trump’s crowd-size answer was about Jan. 6, and Trump called it "the biggest crowd I’ve ever spoken to." Describing his speech to supporters on Jan. 6, 2021, Trump said he spoke to the "same number of people, if not, we had more" than King’s 1963 "I Have a Dream" speech. Here is an image of the crowd during King’s speech: A crowd near the Reflecting Pool listens to Martin Luther King Jr. and other speakers during the March on Washington in 1963.

claim: Republican Senate candidate Dave McCormick “wants to outlaw abortions.”
explanation: But he has said during the 2024 campaign and his campaign website says that he does not support a national abortion ban. Although McCormick has previously made statements that could be considered pro abortion restrictions — such as that he "believes life begins at conception" — he has said during the 2024 campaign cycle that he opposes a national abortion ban. It also says McCormick said he opposes exceptions for abortion restrictions in cases of rape and incest, a claim previous ads also have focused on.

claim: “Hurricane Nadine was a catastrophic Category 5 hurricane that struck Central America and the Bahamas in October 2024.”
explanation: "Hurricane Nadine was a catastrophic Category 5 hurricane that struck Central America and the Bahamas in October 2024," the text says. Still, text spreading online appears to describe a Hurricane Nadine in the past tense. Hurricane Nadine wasn’t a catastrophic Category 5 hurricane, because as of Oct. 10, it never existed.

claim: “Nowhere on her birth certificate does it say that she is BLACK OR AFRICAN. … Kamala Harris is NOT black and never has been.”
explanation: Loomer claimed a birth certificate proves Harris is not Black and never has been because it doesn’t say she is Black or African. The birth certificate does not address Kamala Harris’ race. But Harris’ birth certificate did not include information about her race.

claim: Travis Kelce endorsed Kamala Harris.
explanation: We searched Google and the Nexis news database and found no credible news reports about Kelce endorsing Harris as of Sept. 24. "Breaking: Travis Kelce Follows Taylor Swift’s Footsteps, Supports Harris: ‘Taylor Made the Right Decision,’" a Threads screenshot of a Sept. 15 X post reads. We rate the claim that Travis Kelce endorsed Kamala Harris in mid-September False.

claim: Kamala Harris has adopted the Nazi-rooted phrase “Strength Through Joy” as her campaign slogan.
explanation: But there’s no evidence that Harris has made "strength through joy" her campaign slogan. Harris has not adopted the phrase "strength through joy" as her campaign slogan. PolitiFact searched campaign speech transcripts and news articles and found no instances of Harris using that exact phrase.

claim: “It has just come out that Democrats in Washington and the Democrat Governor’s Office of North Carolina (Roy Cooper) were blocking people and money from coming into North Carolina.”
explanation: "It has just come out that Democrats in Washington and the Democrat Governor’s Office of North Carolina (Roy Cooper) were blocking people and money from coming into North Carolina to help people in desperate need," Trump wrote Oct. 11 on Truth Social. The National File’s Oct. 10 article discussed companywide emails from two Blue Cross Blue Shield in North Carolina employees with updates about the hurricane disaster and guidance about how to safely assist. Trump said, "It has just come out that Democrats in Washington and the Democrat Governor’s Office of North Carolina (Roy Cooper) were blocking people and money from coming into North Carolina."

claim: Says Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz was “banned from future games for flipping off the fans.”
explanation: We found no other evidence, such as credible news stories or public statements from football or university officials, to corroborate the claim that Walz was banned. Tim Walz didn’t flip the bird to football fans at a recent college game, much less get banned from the stadium. Walz also extended a finger — but he’s pointing, not flipping someone off.

claim: In negotiating releases of Americans held abroad, “(I) gave the opposing country NOTHING — and never any cash.”
explanation: In one instance, the U.S. agreed to pay money to North Korea for the release of a U.S. citizen, but a White House official said the money was never sent. However, Bolton, who was not working in the Trump administration at the time of Warmbier’s release, said the U.S. "absolutely" did not pay North Korea any money for the release. National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan said the U.S. did not exchange money in the deal.

claim: With U.S. Customs and Border Protection’s CBP One app, it “takes less than 5 minutes and zero documentation to get approved as an illegal immigrant and be flown to the United States with air tickets paid for by the American taxpayer.”
explanation: Besides asylum seekers, the CBP One app is also used by people who have applied through U.S. The app is used only for scheduling and prescreening; it’s not an asylum or parole application and doesn’t grant migrants U.S. entry. Just as the CBP app itself is not an asylum application, the appointments also are not an asylum application, and border officials don’t decide which people are granted asylum.

claim: “I went down in a helicopter with (Willie Brown). We thought maybe this is the end. We were in a helicopter going to a certain location together and there was an emergency landing.”
explanation: Former President Donald Trump’s tale of an emergency helicopter landing unraveled after one of its main characters, former San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown, told news outlets it never happened. Trump did fly on a helicopter with a different Democrat named Brown — former California Gov. Although we found no news articles about a helicopter crash or emergency landing involving Trump and Brown, we discovered a report about one treacherous helicopter trip involving the former mayor.

claim: Says Simone Biles “announces retirement” and “reveals she is ‘expecting a baby.’”
explanation: Even before her final performance Aug. 5 in the Paris Games, a floor routine that netted her the silver medal, a Facebook post claimed that Biles had announced her retirement and said she was pregnant. Simone Biles is the most decorated gymnast in history and she finished the 2024 Olympics with three gold medals and one silver. "Just Reported that America’s most decorated Olympic gymnast of all time, Simone Biles Announces Retirement at 27 After Securing Gold at Paris Olympics, Reveals she is ‘expecting a baby’ with her husband, Jonathan Owens.

claim: U.S. Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg banned private drones from flying over areas affected by Hurricane Helene.
explanation: The Federal Aviation Administration on Oct. 2 issued a temporary flight restriction in limited parts of the areas Hurricane Helene affected, but lifted the restriction that night. But a Transportation Department spokesperson said the Federal Aviation Administration has not banned drones from providing Hurricane Helene disaster relief and recovery assistance. But a Transportation Department spokesperson said the Federal Aviation Administration is not banning drones from providing Hurricane Helene disaster relief and recovery assistance.

claim: The government is arming “illegal immigrants.”
explanation: We searched Google and the Nexis news database and found no credible reports of the U.S. government supplying immigrants in the country illegally with weapons. The U.S. government is not giving weapons to immigrants in the country illegally, contrary to social media claims. Immigrants in the U.S. illegally are not allowed to own guns, per federal law.

claim: Photo of former President Donald Trump after an assassination attempt was generated by artificial intelligence.
explanation: Vucci’s image was authentic and the moment was widely observed. In the altered image, Trump appears to have six fingers. But these posts claiming it wasn’t a real photo include an altered version of the real image as proof.

claim: An image shows Travis Kelce responding to Elon Musk X post that followed Taylor Swift’s endorsement of Vice President Kamala Harris.
explanation: A post shared by Taylor Swift (@taylorswift) Entrepreneur Elon Musk, who supports former President Donald Trump in the presidential race, responded to Swift’s endorsement on his X platform. A Threads post shared an image that it said shows Kelce responding to a Musk X post. Like Kelce, Swift has not publicly responded to Musk’s X post.

claim: “They create hurricanes via cloud seeding” and “direct them where they want the Hurricane to go!”
explanation: A Facebook post’s claim that Hurricane Milton was created using cloud seeding and steered toward Florida describes something that’s technologically impossible, weather experts said. The "NOAA confirms that there are no weather modification activities that could have resulted in Hurricane Helene or Hurricane Milton," Allen said. If we could geoengineer a hurricane then there would be a lot of other weather that would be dealt with — which isn't happening."

claim: “PA Gov Josh Shapiro isn’t attending the DNC at all.”
explanation: That’s because Shapiro has been at the convention, which started Aug. 19. "PA Gov Josh Shapiro isn’t attending the DNC at all," a screenshot of an X post shared Aug. 19 on Threads said. On Aug. 20, Shapiro took the mic during the DNC’s ceremonial roll call vote, which was broadcast and streamed live, and led the Pennsylvania delegation in submitting their votes for Harris as the Democratic nominee.

claim: "Debate moderators made the false claim to Donald Trump that there is nowhere in the United States where abortion is legal up until birth."
explanation: An Instagram post claiming a moderator falsely told Trump "that there is nowhere in the United States where abortion is legal up until birth" misstates what Davis said. But ABC’s fact-check of Trump on abortion was not about state restrictions on gestational age. "Last night during the ABC debate, two of the participants, otherwise known as the moderators of the debate, made the false claim to Donald Trump that there is nowhere in the United States where abortion is legal up until birth," a man said in a Sept. 11 Instagram video.

claim: “Elon Musk is going to expose Bill Gates soon, says ‘he’s evil.’”
explanation: "Elon Musk is going to expose Bill Gates soon, says ‘he’s evil,’" read text in a Sept. 8 Threads post that showed images of Musk and Gates. "Elon Musk’s shocking claim: Bill Gates is ‘evil’— prepare for the ultimate exposé!," the post said. SpaceXMania, which claims to "bring you the freshest fake news," posted a story on its site Nov. 8 with this headline: "Breaking: Elon Musk exposes Bill Gates on X, says ‘he’s evil.’" The story was labeled "satire" and we found no evidence on Musk’s X account or elsewhere online that he called Gates "evil."

claim: "Teachers and nurses and firefighters are paying a higher tax rate than billionaires and the biggest corporations."
explanation: One study of 342 U.S. large, profitable corporations found they pay an effective tax rate of 14.1%, which is a higher rate than paid by most middle-income workers Harris referred to. Under current law, the 25 highest-earning billionaires paid a 16% tax rate on average, estimates show, while the top 1% of taxpayers paid an average rate more than 25%. Harris said, "Teachers and nurses and firefighters are paying a higher tax rate than billionaires and the biggest corporations."

claim: Republican state Senate candidate Ashlee Adams “campaigned for Mark Robinson and his radical agenda.”
explanation: Asked for evidence that Adams campaigned for Robinson, an Everitt spokesperson said the Adams campaign posted a voter’s guide on its Facebook Aug. 25 that listed Robinson as the Republican gubernatorial candidate. Everitt’s campaign ad claims Adams "campaigned for Mark Robinson and his radical agenda." "Ashlee Adams is working with Mark Robinson to take abortion rights away," a narrator in Everitt’s ad says.

claim: Biden Executive Order 14019 “requires our taxpayer-funded federal agencies to violate the Hatch Act and engage in illegal vote harvesting.”
explanation: The order does not require federal agencies to violate the Hatch Act. The order calls on federal agencies to expand voter registration activities and to do so within the bounds of the law. Tenney claimed that Executive Order 14019 "requires our taxpayer-funded federal agencies to violate the Hatch Act and engage in illegal vote harvesting."

claim: Kamala Harris “supports mandatory gun confiscation.”
explanation: Trump said Harris "supports mandatory gun confiscation." We asked the Harris campaign whether she still supports mandatory assault weapons buybacks. While running in the 2019 presidential primary, Harris said, "I support a mandatory gun buyback program" for assault weapons.

claim: “Project 2025 wants to get rid of NOAA” and the National Weather Service.
explanation: Project 2025 has a few pages about NOAA and the National Weather Service and some of its phrasing is vague. Project 2025 includes about four pages on NOAA and the National Weather Service. Project 2025 would not outright end the National Weather Service.

claim: Video shows footage of Hurricane Helene
explanation: The second clip was taken in Urbandale, Iowa, during a July 2024 tornado, according to local news reports. We tracked the origins of the 10 separate clips included in the compilation:  The first clip featuring a white building and red pickup truck was taken in Nash County, North Carolina, during a July 2023 hurricane, according to WTVD-TV. The third clip of a flying trampoline in a backyard was taken in July 2021 in Rock Hill, South Carolina, according to a video posted on The Weather Channel website.

claim: "Since Vice President Harris and I took office … incomes have risen faster than prices."
explanation: This distinction matters because if Biden had said "wages" had exceeded inflation since he took office, he would have been wrong. After adjusting for inflation, per capita personal income after taxes has risen modestly, once you remove the temporary influx of pandemic-era stimulus cash that distorts the data for January 2021, Biden’s first month in office. "Since Vice President Harris and I took office, our economy has created nearly 16 million jobs, average unemployment has been lower than during any administration in 50 years, and incomes have risen faster than prices," Biden said in an Aug. 2 statement.

claim: Olympic air pistol shooting medalist took up the sport during his divorce and told his ex-wife from the podium, “I want my dog back.”
explanation: Along with the jokes, one story about Dikec making the rounds on social media claims he had a dark backstory to his shooting prowess. One Facebook post shared side-by-side photos of Dikec shooting at the Olympics next to one of him at home with the cat. But the tall tale came from a satirical account called The Sportsmemery, which shared the fake Dikec story in an Aug. 1 post that it described as satire, something the other posts sharing the story omitted.

claim: “MAGA Republicans like Kari Lake support Project 2025, which would raise the retirement age for 73% of Arizonans.”
explanation: On the campaign trail, Lake hasn’t explicitly endorsed Project 2025, but she has appeared in a Project 2025 promotional video. Gallego said, "MAGA Republicans like Kari Lake support Project 2025, which would raise the retirement age for 73% of Arizonans." "MAGA Republicans like Kari Lake support Project 2025, which would raise the retirement age for 73% of Arizonans," Gallego said Aug. 17 on X.

claim: “Taylor Swift faces a 10-game NFL ban following controversial political involvement.”
explanation: We’ve fact-checked misinformation about Swift and her Sept. 10 endorsement of Vice President Kamala Harris, the 2024 Democratic presidential nominee. We’ve fact-checked misinformation about singer-songwriter Taylor Swift and the NFL. One fake news page, SpaceX Fanclub, has been especially prolific with Swift-related posts and features fabricated headlines from Dec. 27 ("NFL franchisees express concerns over Taylor Swift ‘she’s ruining the NFL, and we’re banning her from games’"), Jan. 5 ("Taylor Swift is ruining the NFL and we’re banning her from games"), Feb. 9 ("NFL to ban Taylor Swift from games ‘she’s woke and very distracting’") and Feb. 20 ("NFL franchise owners make it absolutely clear: ‘Taylor Swift ruint the NFL, she’s going to be banned from next season’").

claim: Photo shows a toilet after “some Hezbollah operative blew up.”
explanation: After pagers used by members of the militant group Hezbollah exploded Sept. 17 in Lebanon and Syria, killing more than 30 people and injuring thousands more, an image of a damaged and charred toilet started to spread on social media. We rate claims this photo shows a toilet destroyed after a member of Hezbollah "blew up" False. But the toilet image is old, and from Hong Kong.

claim: Videos show Kamala Harris intoxicated.
explanation: Text above the video said police officers had determined that Harris was intoxicated. The first post shared a video of Harris remaining seated on the first night of the DNC in Chicago as those around her stood and applauded. Many of the social media posts shared clips of Harris’ comments that have gone viral and said they show Harris was drunk — such as when Harris described her mother asking, "You think you just fell out of a coconut tree?"

claim: Charlie Kirk X post about iPhone storage reveals his top app is Grindr.
explanation: A Threads post that claims to show Kirk accidentally revealed in an X post that he uses the gay dating app Grindr used an altered image. An Aug. 27 Threads post shared a screenshot of an X post that showed what it claimed was a social media post from Kirk. The X post claimed Kirk wrote, "Went to check my phone storage and saw the woke gay agenda is alive and well.

claim: Says Colin Kaepernick said he “will go to Russia if not properly respected in the United States.”
explanation: "Colin Kaepernick says he’ll leave Russia if he doesn’t get the respect he deserves in the U.S. - This is SATIRE," said a Sept. 10 Facebook post from SpaceX Fanclub, which notes that "nothing on this page is real." We rate claims Kaepernick said he would leave the United States for Russia False. "Colin Kaepernick: ‘Will go to Russia if not respected properly in the United States,’" a Sept. 13 post said.

claim: In Pompano Beach, Florida, Somali immigrants illegally in the U.S. were in line to get driver’s licenses and “all you need to vote is a driver's license.”
explanation: A video shared on social media claimed to show Somali immigrants in line to get driver’s licenses in Pompano Beach, Florida, and said, "All you need to vote is a driver's license." A video shared across social media showed what it said were hundreds of Somalis illegally in the U.S. lined up to get driver’s licenses in south Florida. Florida law prohibits immigrants in the U.S. illegally from getting driver’s licenses.

claim: “When Tim Walz was asked by his country to go to Iraq, do you know what he did? He dropped out of the Army and allowed his unit to go without him.”
explanation: The Minnesota National Guard said the battalion then received an official order about mobilizing for deployment to Iraq in July 2005, after Walz retired. Walz retired from the Minnesota National Guard in May 2005. Al Bonnifield, who served with Walz in the Minnesota National Guard, told Minnesota Public Radio in 2018 that Walz weighed his retirement from the guard and congressional run "very heavy."

claim: President Joe Biden “killed his first wife.”
explanation: "Yall know Biden killed his first wife and blamed it on a drunk driver and the man hadn’t even been drinking and the police reports have been lost," the July 18 post said. We rate claims that Biden killed his first wife Pants on Fire! Nealia Biden, 30, was driving the family’s station wagon Dec. 18, 1972, when she and Biden’s infant daughter, Naomi, were killed in a collision.

claim: “Chiefs' Coach Andy Reid criticizes Taylor Swift: ‘You’re not a good role model.’”
explanation: "Chiefs coach Andy Reid confronts Taylor Swift ‘You’re not a good role model,’" said a July 1 post on the SpaceX Fanclub Facebook account. "Chiefs' Coach Andy Reid criticizes Taylor Swift: ‘You’re not a good role model,’" a Sept. 17 Facebook post said. "I think it's great for him," Reid said.

claim: “Donald Trump posted this photo of Taylor Swift saying that she was crying because she lost over $150 million worth of merchandise.”
explanation: "So, Donald Trump posted this photo of Taylor Swift saying that she was crying because she lost over $150 million worth of merchandise boycotting because she endorsed Kamala Harris," a person in the video said. "Trump posts photo of Taylor Swift crying," read text in the video that also included a screenshot of an X post from an account called "Donald J. Trump News." Finally, the images of Swift used in the X post struck a nerve for some Swift fans and distressed the mother of a boy who died from cancer before his fourth birthday and inspired Swift to write a song about him.

claim: “Even before the pandemic, (Donald Trump) lost manufacturing jobs, by most people’s estimates at least 200,000.”
explanation: About 200,000 manufacturing jobs were lost during Trump’s entire tenure, not just the prepandemic period. But the 200,000 jobs figure she cites includes manufacturing job losses during Trump’s entire presidency, not just the prepandemic period. Bureau of Labor Statistics data shows that manufacturing sector employment fell by 48,000 from its prepandemic peak in January 2019 to February 2020, the month before the pandemic hit the U.S. That’s a quarter of the number of jobs Harris said were lost before the pandemic.

claim: "Tim Walz firmó una ley para dar licencia de conducir a inmigrantes ilegales en Minnesota".
explanation: La ley entró en vigor el 1 de octubre de 2023. La población de Minnesota es de unos 5.7 millones de habitantes. obtener una licencia de conducir estándar o tarjeta de identificación de Minnesota.

claim: “ABC lost $27M in ad revenue after advertisers pulled ads from the network after the way they hosted the debate" on Sept. 10.
explanation: We searched using Google and the Nexis news database and found no credible reports that ABC lost advertisers or ad revenue because of its handling of the Sept. 10 presidential debate in Philadelphia. He has said that, if he were Florida’s governor, he would have signed the state’s current six-week abortion ban, which includes exceptions for rape and incest through 15 weeks of pregnancy and the pregnant woman’s health and life. explanation: El expresidente sufrió un intento de asesinato el 13 de julio en un mitin en Butler, Pensilvania, pero Trump dijo que ya se recuperó de una herida de bala en su oreja derecha. explanation: We rate claims this photo shows a child found in Elko County, Nevada, by Deputy Ryan Braidley False. The Elko County Sheriff’s Office confirmed to PolitiFact that no Ryan Braidley works there. "Deputy" isn’t typically a title at police departments such as Elko’s, but no Ryan Braidley works there, either.

claim: “Gordon Ramsay calls Tim Walz a ‘woke creep,’ throws him out of Hell’s Kitchen.”
explanation: "Gordon Ramsay calls Tim Walz a ‘woke creep,’ throws him out of Hell’s Kitchen," a Sept. 6 Facebook post said, referring to a Ramsay restaurant with seven locations across the country, including Washington, D.C. A Facebook page that posts satirical content shared the claim Sept. 4 on its account with one major caveat: it was clearly "rated satire," whereas the Sept. 6 Facebook post included no such label. This post was flagged as part of Meta’s efforts to combat false news and misinformation on its News Feed.

claim: Photo shows Gatlinburg, Tennessee, flooded on Sept. 30, 2024.
explanation: That’s because "this is an AI photo and not real," the city of Gatlinburg said on X in response to an account sharing the image and wrongly describing it as showing Gatlinburg on Sept. 28. We rate claims this is an authentic photo of Gatlinburg flooded False. A few days later, the city shared a post from the city’s convention and visitors bureau, which noted Gatlinburg wasn’t even flooded.

claim: ABC News fired presidential debate moderators David Muir and Linsey Davis.
explanation: The Facebook post links to an article that said ABC News released a statement Sept. 11 that the network fired Muir and Davis for fact-checking Trump and asking Vice President Kamala Harris’ questions. We rate the claim that ABC News fired debate moderators Muir and Davis Pants on Fire! We searched Google and the Nexis news database and found no reports about ABC News firing Muir and Davis.

claim: “Kansas City Chiefs CEO bans Taylor Swift from attending games, calling her the team’s ‘biggest distraction.’”
explanation: In August, Bloomberg News reported that Hunt said Swift had helped to boost the Chiefs’ fan base by 30%. The Chiefs have issued no press releases about a Swift ban, and we found no public statements from Hunt saying as much. And this particular new claim about Swift and Chiefs CEO Clark Hunt has appeared on at least one Facebook page that notes "nothing on this page is real."

claim: Nevada Sen. Jacky Rosen said the Biden administration did a "tremendous job" on the U.S. military’s Afghanistan withdrawal.
explanation: Brown said Rosen said the Biden administration did a "tremendous job" on the Afghanistan withdrawal. We asked Brown for evidence Rosen said Biden did a "tremendous job" on the withdrawal. Rosen campaign spokesperson Johanna Warshaw said Rosen’s "tremendous job" comment referred to officials working quickly to abide by the Aug. 31, 2021, deadline to get Americans out of the country quickly as the Taliban took over.

claim: "In Springfield (Ohio), they're eating the dogs, the people that came in, they're eating the cats. They're eating, they're eating the pets of the people that live there.”
explanation: Springfield Mayor Rob Rue at a Sept. 10 city commission meeting reiterated that there were no credible or specific claims about Haitian immigrants stealing and eating pets. Trump said that in Springfield, Ohio, Haitian immigrants are "eating the pets of the people that live there." A city spokesperson and Springfield police said they have received no credible reports that pets are being abducted and eaten by the immigrants.

claim: “BREAKING: Illegal Aliens in San Diego, California, tried to hijack 2 school buses filled with children.”
explanation: Although groups of people approached buses on two separate occasions, accounts from Jamul-Dulzura Union School District Superintendent Liz Bystedt, the San Diego County sheriff’s office and local news reports said there was no attempted hijacking. On Aug. 27 and 28, groups of people approached Jamul-Dulzura Union School District buses on Highway 94 in San Diego County. The claims trace to events Aug. 27 and 28 when groups of people approached two Jamul-Dulzura Union School District buses on Highway 94 in Dulzura, an unincorporated part of San Diego County.

claim: Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz signed a bill “redefining ‘sexual orientation’ to include pedophiles.”
explanation: Before the bill passed, Republican state Rep. Harry Niska added language to the bill that said: "The physical or sexual attachment to children by an adult is not a protected class under this chapter." The bill amended the definition of "sexual orientation" to remove a line that said: "‘Sexual orientation’ does not include a physical or sexual attachment to children by an adult." RNC Research, an X account run by former President Donald Trump’s campaign and the Republican National Committee, posted Aug. 6 that Walz signed a bill into law "removing ‘physical or sexual attachment to children by an adult’ from (Minnesota’s) human rights law — redefining ‘sexual orientation’ to include pedophiles."

claim: "Kamala Harris aboga por censurar X en Estados Unidos al estilo de Brasil si es elegida presidenta en noviembre”.
explanation: Twitter suspendió la cuenta de Trump el 8 de enero de 2021, después de que usara la plataforma para alentar a sus seguidores a protestar por los resultados de las elecciones de 2020 el 6 de enero de 2021. La misma regla tiene que aplicarse, que es que tiene que haber una responsabilidad que recaiga sobre estos sitios de redes sociales para que comprendan su poder. La misma regla tiene que aplicarse, que es que tiene que haber una responsabilidad que recaiga sobre estos sitios de redes sociales para que comprendan su poder.

claim: “During Covid, Tim Walz rationed access to monoclonal antibody treatments based on skin color.”
explanation: Minnesota later designed a scoring system first used in December 2021 that assigned people points, on a scale of zero to 25, based on categories of clinical risk from COVID-19, The program used the Mayo Clinic’s Monoclonal Antibody Screening Score, but added categories for pregnant women and Black, Indigenous and people of color as risk factors. Minnesota’s health department cited the FDA’s guidance in 2021 emergency-use approvals for monoclonal antibody treatments that "in addition to certain underlying health conditions, race and ethnicity "may also place individual patients at high risk for progression to severe COVID-19." Kirk’s claim that Minnesota rationed health care by skin color has elements of truth in that a scoring system awarded patients who were Black, Indigenous or people of color 2 points, the same as patients with diabetes or cardiovascular disease and more than a patient with hypertension.

claim: “Netflix stock tumbles almost 40%” after the company donated to Kamala Harris’ campaign.
explanation: We rate claims that Netflix’s stock tumbled after the company donated to Harris’ presidential campaign False. Spoiler alert: Netflix’s stock didn’t plummet 40% after the company donated to Vice President Kamala Harris’ presidential campaign, contrary to viral social media posts. But the article and social media posts falsely claim that the donation came from the company, rather than Hastings.

claim: “In 12 states, children born alive after a failed abortion have no legal protection, and in three more states children born alive after an abortion had legal rights that governors — like Tim Walz — repealed.”
explanation: Perkins said, "In 12 states, children born alive after a failed abortion have no legal protection, and in three more states children born alive after an abortion had legal rights that governors — like Tim Walz — repealed." In a Sept. 11 Facebook post, Tony Perkins, president of the anti-abortion Family Research Council, wrote, "In 12 states, children born alive after a failed abortion have no legal protection, and in three more states children born alive after an abortion had legal rights that governors — like Tim Walz — repealed." Every person who is born has protections under federal and state laws.

claim: Vice President Kamala Harris “endorsed free taxpayer-funded government health care for all illegal aliens.”
explanation: Harris has not expressly said she supports free, taxpayer-supported health coverage for immigrants who are in the country illegally. Harris signaled in 2019 that her Medicare for All proposal would cover immigrants who are in the country illegally. Republicans have sought to portray Harris as extreme on immigration and assert that  she supports free, taxpayer-funded health benefits for immigrants who are in the country illegally.

claim: Says Elon Musk posted on X, “Any harassment of Trump supporters using the term ‘weird’ will be punished.”
explanation: An Aug. 7 Instagram post sharing an image of the purported X post was flagged as part of Meta’s efforts to combat false news and misinformation on its News Feed. The image in the Instagram post includes no such logo. "‘Weird’ is being used as a slur against Trump supporters, and it will not be tolerated on this platform," reads what looks like a July 30 X post from Musk.

claim: “Taylor Swift’s manager confirms: ‘Ticket sales are dead after Harris endorsement backlash.”
explanation: We rate claims this is an authentic quote from Swift’s manager False. We also found no credible evidence, such as news stories or public statements, that anyone who works with Swift has said ticket sales are dead because of the endorsement. We searched for the purported quote from Swift’s manager and found it originated on a self-described satire site.

claim: “A staffer reveals that Kamala Harris doesn’t actually own a gun.”
explanation: The exchange in the video was significantly sped up and captions appearing Elrod as she speaks reads: "She doesn’t own a firearm." The original footage of this exchange makes clear that Elrod doesn’t say "she doesn’t own a firearm." We rate claims a staffer said Harris doesn’t own a gun Pants on Fire!

claim: Mike Rogers “left Michigan to trade on his D.C. connections, helping Chinese tech companies get access to the U.S.”
explanation: In an ad, Slotkin’s campaign said Rogers was "helping Chinese companies get access to the U.S."  Rogers worked for AT&T while it was pursuing deals with Chinese phone companies to sell their devices in the U.S. Rogers worked for American tech companies that had connections to Huawei — including AT&T and Nokia. In the letter, which the Rogers campaign provided to PolitiFact, Rogers’ lawyers wrote that Rogers "has never worked for any Chinese tech companies, including ZTE and Huawei."

claim: Kamala Harris voted in favor of passing a law in 2022 to tax tips.
explanation: The claim that the IRS would hire 87,000 IRS agents came from a 2021 Department of Treasury report that said the IRS would use the $80 billion from the Inflation Reduction Act to hire 86,852 full-time employees. The IRS did propose a tip reporting program in 2023 that would let service industry employers report tips voluntarily to help with tax compliance. And the IRS tip reporting program is a voluntary program that would replace existing tax compliance programs.

claim: “There’s no such thing as menopause.”
explanation: Numerous clinics, groups of health care professionals and medical research organizations say menopause exists, and generally define it as the point at which a woman has naturally gone 12 months without a menstrual period. Cleveland Clinic: "Menopause is a point in time when a person has gone 12 consecutive months without a menstrual period. Menopause is a natural part of aging and marks the end of your reproductive years."

claim: “Sen. Jacky Rosen voted to increase taxes on families making less than $75,000 a year.”
explanation: A One Nation ad said Rosen "voted to increase taxes on families making less than $75,000 a year." Republican-backed groups making claims similar to the One Nation ad have relied on a 2022 Joint Committee on Taxation Inflation Reduction Act analysis that showed an increased tax burden in every bracket. One Nation has released three other ads since June, all saying Rosen voted to increase taxes on families making less than $75,000.

claim: "Missouri registered 78,421 in just one week of February of this year. Out of that number, 23,253 were dead people!"
explanation: The Help America Vote Verification database shows the number of verification requests sent by a state’s election office to confirm a person’s eligibility to vote — not the number of people who registered to vote in a given week — a Social Security Administration spokesperson said in a statement sent to PolitiFact. It does not tally the number of people who are registered to vote or who are trying to register to vote. "Under the Help America Vote Act, when a voter registrant does not have a driver’s license, states are permitted to submit the voter registrant’s name, date of birth and last four digits of their Social Security number to the Social Security Administration for verification," the statement said.

claim: Haitians are responsible for the disappearance of 16 cats in Bangor, Maine.
explanation: The post includes video from an Aug. 29 News Center Maine broadcast about "at least 16 cats" that had disappeared from a Bangor neighborhood, Fairmount. McAmbley also shared a statement from Bruen, who said she believes both humans possibly stealing cats and wildlife are to blame for the missing cats, which "must be close to 20 by now." "Bangor’s animal control officer, Trisha Bruen, said she believes the cats were killed by wildlife," the reporter says in the segment.

claim: Pallets of bricks were left all over the streets of Chicago before the Democratic National Convention.
explanation: PolitiFact rated a similar claim False about pallets of bricks being found near locations of DNC-related protests. PolitiFact fact-checked those claims in 2020, finding that officials in cities across the U.S. said there was no connection between pallets of bricks and Black Lives Matter protests. The posts also say that bricks were found near Black Lives Matter protests in 2020 to incite violence.

claim: Says U.S. Sen. Tammy Baldwin “has done absolutely nothing” about the fentanyl crisis.
explanation: Hovde went on to say that Baldwin was merely one in a long list of co-sponsors on a recent fentanyl bill that was introduced by a Republican lawmaker. Hovde claimed Baldwin "has done absolutely nothing" to address the fentanyl crisis in Wisconsin. Hovde’s campaign argued that on the bill that passed, Baldwin was not a major factor.

claim: “Dave McCormick is fully against abortion.”
explanation: But during the 2024 campaign, McCormick has said he would not support a national abortion ban. During the 2024 campaign, though, McCormick has softened his abortion position and said if elected, he would oppose a national abortion ban if it were proposed. The article’s author wrote: "David McCormick — who's facing a heated primary with his Trump-backed opponent, Mehmet Oz — said during a debate in Harrisburg last month he's fully against all scenarios involving abortion, apart from ‘in the very rare instances there should be exceptions for the life of the mother.’"   During that 2022 debate, the moderator asked McCormick whether he believes there should be exceptions to abortion laws for rape, incest and when the pregnant woman’s life is at risk.

claim: “Mark Wahlberg y Mel Gibson invierten 500 millones de dólares para el primer estudio de producción de la industria centrado en los valores tradicionales”.
explanation: Una publicación en Facebook dice que los actores Mark Wahlberg y Mel Gibson invirtieron millones de dólares en un estudio de producción con valores tradicionales. "Mark Wahlberg y Mel Gibson invierten 500 millones de dólares para el primer estudio de producción de la industria centrado en los valores tradicionales", dice la publicación del 21 de agosto. La imagen en la publicación en Facebook tiene como titular en inglés la supuesta noticia de que Wahlberg y Gibson invirtieron en un estudio.

claim: “Prices are up because these corporations are scheming to drive them up.”
explanation: Barrett, of Cornell University, said evidence that corporate price markups are causing rising prices has "grown over time." There is evidence that corporate profits are rising faster than inflation. However, it also noted that food and beverage retailers’ annual profits — or the amount they make above total costs — remain high, which the report said "casts doubt on assertions that rising prices at the grocery store" are because of retailers’ rising costs.

claim: Image shows “P Diddy with Kamala Harris.”
explanation: But one Threads post mischaracterizes an image of Vice President and 2024 Democratic presidential nominee Kamala Harris. "Here is P Diddy with Kamala Harris," text above the image says. The person in the image isn’t Combs but talk show host Montel Williams, whom Harris once dated.

claim: “Portugal lanza monedas de 7 euros para honrar al legendario futbolista Cristiano Ronaldo”.
explanation: Las dos monedas conmemorativas en circulación son una de los 50 años del 25 de abril de 1974, la Revolución de los Claveles, que acabó con 48 años de dictadura en el país. Y otra de la participación de Portugal en los Juegos Olímpicos de París. Siwei Lyu, profesor de la universidad de Buffalo, dijo que las imágenes presentan muestras de inteligencia artificial.

claim: 2023 FEMA webinar shows the agency is prioritizing its relief efforts around LGBTQ+ people
explanation: X posts shared a clip of a 2023 FEMA webinar and cited it as evidence that FEMA is prioritizing LGBTQ+ people in its disaster response. This webinar was a discussion among FEMA and non-FEMA representatives about improving disaster preparedness for LGBTQ+ people; it was not about FEMA’s general disaster response. But this video does not show that FEMA has prioritized LGBTQ+ people in its relief efforts.

claim: CNN reported that the Apalachee High School shooting suspect was motivated by a “lack of trans acceptance.”
explanation: The CNN article did not use this wording and by the time this Instagram post was made, CNN had clarified what the Discord account said about transgender people. CNN also reported in that article that the Discord account "expressed frustration with the acceptance of transgender people," according to a Sept. 5 archive of the CNN article page. A Sept. 7 Instagram post shared a screenshot of an X post that claimed the suspect was driven by a "lack of trans acceptance," citing CNN’s reporting.

claim: “El Proyecto 2025 quiere deshacerse de la NOAA” y del Servicio Nacional de Meteorología.
explanation: Rick Thoman, un especialista climático de Alaska en la Universidad de Alaska Fairbanks, dijo que el lenguaje ambiguo del Proyecto 2025 hizo difícil evaluar si este llama a la eliminación de la NOAA y el Servicio Nacional de Meteorología. ¿Qué dice el Proyecto 2025 sobre la NOAA y el Servicio Nacional de Meteorología de Estados Unidos? El Proyecto 2025 incluye alrededor de cuatro páginas sobre la NOAA y el Servicio Nacional de Meteorología.

claim: Kamala Harris "let in the 13,099 convicted murderers and opposes all efforts to find them and to remove them."
explanation: Immigration and Customs Enforcement does not provide the year people who were convicted of crimes entered the U.S. People cannot be indefinitely in immigration detention: Immigration law requires people convicted of aggravated felonies, such as homicide, be detained. There are several reasons why people convicted of crimes are not in immigration detention.

claim: “BREAKING: Apalachee High School shooter has been identified as non-binary trans girl Samantha Hyde.”
explanation: Authorities identified the suspect in the Apalachee High School shooting as 14-year-old Colt Gray, a student at the Winder, Georgia, school. We rate the claim that the Apalachee High School shooter was identified as "Samantha Hyde" Pants on Fire! That Jackson County sheriff’s office report, which identified Gray as male, said nothing about Gray being nonbinary or transgender.

claim: “Elon Musk has announced his first robot girlfriend, with artificial intelligence.”
explanation: The image of Musk seated in a restaurant with a humanoid robot is not real. "Elon Musk has announced his first robot girlfriend, with artificial intelligence. Tech 4 Peace, an Iraqi fact-checking outlet and signatory of the International Fact-Checking Network, also reported that the image of Musk with the supposed girlfriend robot was created with artificial intelligence.

claim: Of Bernie Moreno, “Now, he’s arguing for a national abortion ban, no exceptions.”
explanation: Brown’s campaign said in opposing the abortion access amendment, Moreno voted to uphold the six-week abortion ban with no exceptions for rape or incest. When he ran in Ohio’s 2022 Republican primary for Senate, Moreno said he opposed exceptions to abortion bans. In his 2024 campaign, Moreno has said he supports federal limits on abortion after 15 weeks, with exceptions.

claim: "Mark Zuckerberg, CEO de Meta, ha retirado la verificación” de Nicolás Maduro en Facebook e Instagram.
explanation: Captura de pantalla de la página de Facebook de Nicolás Maduro del 1 de abril de 2022 en Archive.today. Captura de pantalla de la página de Instagram de Nicolás Maduro del 13 de noviembre de 2020 en Wayback Machine. Archivos de la cuenta de Instagram de Maduro de 2017, 2019 y 2020, no muestran el sello de verificación.

claim: JD Vance holds “anti-marriage-equality views.”
explanation: "I don't think it's actually about gay marriage, it is not about same-sex marriage or same-sex equality," Vance said. Vance and Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg contradicted each other when asked about Vance’s views of gay marriage. During an Oct. 10, 2022, televised Senate race debate between Vance and Rep. Tim Ryan, D-Ohio, Vance said he opposed the Respect for Marriage Act, then pending before Congress.

claim: On June 7, 2011, Kamala Harris was involved in a San Francisco hit-and-run crash that injured a woman named Alicia Brown.
explanation: A viral video claimed that Harris was involved in a June 7, 2011, hit-and-run crash in San Francisco that injured a woman named Alicia Brown. San Francisco Police Department spokesperson Allison Maxie said the agency found no calls for service or other reports involving a hit-and-run or car crash in the vicinity of the intersection of Post and Jones streets on or around this date in 2011. In video clips shared Sept. 4 on X, a woman identified as "Alicia Brown" claimed Harris, the Democratic presidential nominee, drove a car that struck and injured her June 7, 2011.

claim: The apparent assassination attempt against former President Donald Trump on Sept. 15, 2024, was “staged.”
explanation: Social media users claimed the apparent assassination attempt against Trump on Sept. 15 was "staged." Soon after U.S. Secret Service agents intervened to stop a second assassination attempt against former President Donald Trump on Sept. 15, social media users started spreading conspiracy theories about the incident, including that it was staged. In July, when a gunman opened fire on Trump during a Butler, Pennsylvania, campaign rally and a bullet grazed Trump’s ear, social media users also falsely claimed that assassination attempt was staged.

claim: Video shows former President Donald Trump freezing up.
explanation: Thank you, thank you very much, thank you. Thank you. Thank you."

claim: “Biden Announces: ‘2.4 billion more to Ukraine’ but ‘no more aid for Hurricane Helene.’”
explanation: A reporter asked whether there were more resources the federal government could be giving states, and Biden answered no and said the administration had preplanned a significant amount of aid that was already being deployed. We found other posts claiming that Biden said no more aid would be coming for states affected by the storm, with some tying it to aid for Ukraine. Social media posts claimed that Biden "announced" there would be billions in aid for Ukraine but no more aid for areas affected by Hurricane Helene.

claim: Vice President Kamala Harris wore NOVA H1 audio earrings in the Sept. 10, 2024, presidential debate.
explanation: We rate the claim that Harris was wearing the NOVA H1 earphone earrings during the presidential debate Pants on Fire! The NOVA H1 earrings and the earrings Harris wore during the debate may look similar because of a pearl in both designs, but upon closer inspection, they have important differences. Kelley said on her blog that Harris wore the same earrings during the presidential debate.

claim: Charleroi, Pennsylvania, “has grown by 2,000% due to an influx in migrants.”
explanation: Town officials said 700 to 2,000 immigrants have moved there over recent years, and there has been a significant rise in the number of students who are learning English in the school district. "Take the small town of Charleroi, which has grown by 2,000% due to an influx in migrants," McCormick said in a recent post on X. McCormick said the Pennsylvania town of Charleroi has "grown by 2,000% due to an influx in migrants."

claim: "ÚLTIMA HORA Río Nilo se pinta de rojo sangre".
explanation: Portavoces del Servicio Nacional de Turismo de Chile y de Paricota Tours, una agencia privada de turismo en Chile, confirmaron a PolitiFact que la imagen de la publicación en Facebook mostraba la Laguna Roja. En la página del gobierno chileno Chile.travel, encontramos una imagen de la creadora de contenido Victoria Ansaldo con la misma ropa que en la imagen compartida en la publicación en Facebook. Al hacer una búsqueda de imagen inversa de la publicación en Facebook, encontramos diversas páginas sobre la Laguna Roja en Chile.

claim: “iPhones exploding in Lebanon blowing up random people.”
explanation: "iPhones exploding in Lebanon blowing up random people," said an X post accompanied by what looks like an exploded iPhone. But the image of the damaged iPhone is not from the Lebanon attacks. We rate the claim "iPhones exploding in Lebanon blowing up random people," False.

claim: "Kid Rock heads to North Carolina with Millions in supplies. Taylor Swift Nowhere to be Found.”
explanation: The claim that Kid Rock has donated millions in supplies in North Carolina while Taylor Swift was nowhere to be seen originated on a satirical website, but many users are sharing it as real. We found no credible news articles in a search of Google and the Nexis news database that Kid Rock has donated "millions in supplies" to North Carolina storm victims. Some social media posts are praising singer Kid Rock and chastising singer Taylor Swift for their responses to Hurricane Helene.

claim: “Video shows Kamala (Harris) responding to someone talking through her earrings that she allegedly wore during the Trump vs. Harris debate.”
explanation: "Video shows Kamala responding to someone talking through her earrings that she allegedly wore during the Trump vs. Harris debate," the Sept. 29 Instagram post said. During the debate, Harris wore pearl earrings. Let’s get a few things out of the way: The video doesn't show Harris talking to someone through her earrings, which are different than the pair she wore during the debate.

claim: “Breaking: Pete Buttigieg reveals that he is HIV-positive.”
explanation: This claim about Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg is entirely invented, but stereotypes about gay men and HIV are part of a much older playbook. Gay and bisexual men still remain at high risk for contracting HIV, but people can take many steps to prevent infection. Although anyone can contract HIV, the stigma for gay men persists today.

claim: “The transgender thing is incredible... your kid goes to school and comes home a few days later with an operation. The school decides what’s going to happen with your child."
explanation: Trump’s campaign cited school policies that do not require teachers to notify parents if a student is transgender, but these policies do not mean a child can be given medical care or surgical care without parental consent. We asked National Association of School Nurses President Kate King what kind of medical care school nurses may give. Schools do not provide medical care without parental consent, let alone surgery.

claim: “Oprah is a sex trafficker. She’s been caught and now has to be escorted around” by U.S. marshals
explanation: We rate the claim that Winfrey is a sex trafficker who must be escorted around by U.S. marshals Pants on Fire! "She’s been caught and now has to be escorted around by the U.S. A U.S.

claim: “Donald Trump said he was going to allow Medicare to negotiate drug prices. He never did. We did.”
explanation: More importantly, the Most Favored Nation model did not authorize the government to negotiate prescription drug prices with manufacturers — the policy Trump promised to implement. As a presidential candidate in 2016, Donald Trump promised to let the government negotiate prescription drug prices directly with pharmaceutical companies. Harris, therefore, is correct that Trump never was able to open Medicare up to drug negotiations despite his sweeping campaign promises.

claim: “Unlike other amendments, Amendment 4 has no definitions. … Without definitions these words can mean almost anything.”
explanation: An anti-Amendment 4 ad in Florida says, "Unlike other amendments, Amendment 4 has no definitions. "Unlike other amendments, Amendment 4 has no definitions," the narrator said. "Unlike other amendments, Amendment 4 has no definitions," the narrator said in a Vote No on 4 ad that aired during the Sept. 10 presidential debate.

claim: The World Health Organization ordered governments to prepare for “mega lockdown” because of an mpox strain.
explanation: The framework encourages countries to control mpox outbreaks, advance mpox research and limit transmission between animals and people. But the WHO has made no announcements about mpox lockdowns. The full article says the WHO has ordered governments "to prepare to initiate tough new lockdowns" after declaring mpox a public health emergency.

claim: El expresidente Donald Trump “tiene la intención de promulgar lo que, en efecto, es un impuesto nacional sobre las ventas…que elevaría los precios para las familias de clase media a casi $4,000 al año”.
explanation: El Instituto Urbano-Centro de Política Fiscal de la Institución Brookings, un grupo de expertos con sede en Washington D.C., calculó que los aranceles del 10% y el 60% reducirían colectivamente los ingresos medios después de impuestos de los hogares estadounidenses en unos $1,800. Durante su discurso de aceptación el 22 de agosto en la Convención Nacional Demócrata en Chicago, Harris también dijo que Trump "tiene la intención de promulgar lo que, en efecto, es un impuesto nacional sobre las ventas — llámelo impuesto Trump — que elevaría los precios de las familias de clase media en casi $4,000 al año". Aunque los aranceles se recaudan por separado de los impuestos, la mayoría de los economistas dicen que gran parte de su impacto se traslada a los consumidores.

claim: Video shows “the bunker-busting bombs that ended the lives of (Hassan) Nasrallah and Hezbollah’s leadership.”
explanation: Another bombing of a residential building was shared Aug. 27 on X with a caption saying it was from the Nuseirat camp in Gaza. The X video that claims it shows the strike on Nasralla also contains other footage of Gaza airstrikes, including: A man and a child run as a building behind them is hit by a bomb, shared Aug. 17 on Facebook and labeled as being in Gaza. A video of a residential building was shared on Instagram in February with a caption saying it was from Gaza.

claim: "El crimen violento aumentó bajo Donald Trump".
explanation: Después de disminuir durante los primeros tres años de la presidencia de Trump, el aumento de la tasa de crímenes violentos en 2020 (su último año del republicano en el cargo) fue lo suficientemente grande como para borrar las disminuciones de los años anteriores de su mandato. Sin embargo, incluso considerando el repunte de 2020, la tasa de crímenes violentos en el último año de Trump fue aún más baja que en el último año de su predecesor, el presidente demócrata Barack Obama. La última parte de la declaración de Walz se refería a la condena de Trump en mayo de 2024 por 34 cargos de falsificación de registros comerciales en un esquema para encubrir un pago de dinero secreto a la actriz porno Stormy Daniels previo a las elecciones presidenciales de 2016.

claim: Kamala Harris campaign ad “features a mother expressing regret for not having an abortion.”
explanation: "BREAKING: New Kamala Harris campaign ad features a mother expressing regret for not having an abortion," the caption of an Oct. 2 X post read. The voice in the fake ad "doesn’t sound quite like Harris in terms of the cadence or the intonations," he said. Harris didn’t release an ad that "features a mother expressing regret for not having an abortion."

claim: Patents dating back to the 1800s show that people can control the weather.
explanation: Experts told PolitiFact that they knew of no technology that allows anyone to control the weather or create a hurricane, and denied that the meme’s patents proved weather control is possible. Our review of some of the patents found that not only do they not prove humans could control weather features such as hurricanes, but some appeared to have no direct connection to weather technology. Experts said they knew of no technology that could create or control hurricanes.

claim: Hurricane Milton article is evidence they "control and plan these storms."
explanation: The Convoy of Hope article also was updated Oct. 7 to note that the hypothetical article had been taken down now that a real storm named Hurricane Milton was expected to hit Florida. An Instagram post claimed that an article about the effects of Hurricane Milton published before the storm hit the U.S. is evidence that storms are controlled and planned. The Hypothetical Hurricanes article about Milton now says the original article was deleted Oct. 7 to prevent misinformation.

claim: Sen. JD Vance admitted he has a ‘rent-a-dog’ from the Trump campaign to make him “seem like a dog person.”
explanation: The video shows Vance telling Carlson, "He’s actually a rent-a-dog that was given to me by the campaign to make me seem like I’m a dog fan." Vance did not call his dog a "rent-a-dog." Vance said his family has had Atlas since he was a puppy.

claim: Photo shows missing couple Raymond Peterson and his wife, Sophie.
explanation: Other Facebook posts featuring the same photo and narrative say Raymond Peterson and his wife Sophie were last seen in other places around the United States, such as "Northeast Montana." We rate claims this photo shows Raymond Peterson and his wife, Stephanie Menard, a couple missing from Texas, or any other state, False. One such post said the pair had been last seen in Wise County, Texas.

claim: Vice President Kamala Harris “cast the tiebreaking votes that caused the worst inflation in American history, costing a typical American family $28,000.”
explanation: Trump said Harris "cast the tiebreaking votes that caused the worst inflation in American history, costing a typical American family $28,000." However, most economists also agree that the American Rescue Plan exacerbated inflation but was not the sole cause. During a Sept. 7 rally in Mosinee, Wisconsin, Trump said that as vice president, Kamala Harris — his Democratic opponent — "cast the tiebreaking votes that caused the worst inflation in American history, costing a typical American family $28,000."

claim: Mike Rogers supported “laws that could eliminate IVF and birth control.”
explanation: Slotkin said Rogers supported "laws that could eliminate IVF and birth control." IVF could still be legal under personhood laws, but experts said the procedure would likely be more expensive and have lower success rates, and providers could exit the industry because of liability risk. All that said, the bills Rogers supported would not have banned either IVF or birth control.

claim: “Taylor Swift forced to cancel Eras Tour dates following endorsement backlash.”
explanation: We rate the claim that Swift was forced to cancel Eras tour dates after endorsing Harris False. We could not find any news reports about Swift canceling tour dates after her Harris endorsement. "Taylor Swift Forced to Cancel Eras Tour Dates Following Endorsement Backlash: ‘Only 2,300 Tickets Sold,’" read a Sept. 16 Facebook post.

claim: Project 2025 would “cut” the Federal Emergency Management Agency and “kill federal-backed flood insurance.”
explanation: Project 2025’s proposed FEMA changes include raising the per capita threshold for providing FEMA public assistance, terminating its grants, replacing the National Flood Insurance Program with privatized insurance and changing FEMA’s cost-share so that federal government covers less of the cost for smaller disaster response and recovery. But Project 2025 said FEMA grants should be terminated and states "should bear the costs of their particularized programs" instead. Social media posts said Project 2025 would "cut FEMA" and "kill federal-backed flood insurance."

claim: Says Kamala Harris tweeted, “It’s BLACK LIVES MATTER, not ‘Biden Loves Minors!’”
explanation: But Vice President Kamala Harris didn’t post on X reacting to calls to prosecute Cheatle. "I am DISGUSTED by @BoLoudon’s SEXIST call to prosecute our first DEI Secret Service Woman Director," reads what looks like an X post from Harris, referring to a conservative commentator and friend of Trump’s son, Barron. "Bo is a 17 year old RACIST — it’s BLACK LIVES MATTER, not ‘Biden Loves Minors!’ DO NOT follow him!’" A July 28 Instagram post sharing an image of the purported X post was flagged as part of Meta’s efforts to combat false news and misinformation on its News Feed.

claim: Four government agencies donated nearly $900,000 of taxpayer money to Kamala Harris’ presidential campaign.
explanation: Although these four government agencies are listed among the top contributors to Harris’ campaign on Open Secrets’ website, it doesn’t mean the agencies themselves donated to her campaign. As of July 29, Open Secrets reported the following contributions to Harris’ campaign from people affiliated with these government agencies: Defense Department: $213,460 Health and Human Services: $203,574 State Department: $197,640 Veterans Affairs: $217,420 Government agencies, including the Defense Department and the Department of Veterans Affairs, are also listed among the top contributors to former President Donald Trump’s presidential campaign on Open Secrets’ website. Under each of these government agencies, Open Secrets’ website says individuals were the source of the political contributions.. On these top contributor pages, Open Secrets further explains why and how it uses donors’ employer and occupation information.

claim: A 15-year-old named “Graci Mae Thompson” is missing.
explanation: In two instances, PolitiFact found that the users had posted about missing children before, then changed those posts to advertise properties for sale. Facebook posts have sounded the alarm over the disappearance of a 15-year-old named Graci Mae Thompson, who has supposedly been missing since July 22. But PolitiFact found no evidence of a girl named Graci Mae Thompson who is now reported missing.

claim: Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that Kamala Harris used to be a man named Kamal Aroush.
explanation: A screenshot purporting to be from Trump’s Truth Social account and shared on Threads contains a photo of Harris and another digitally altered image of her supposedly as a man. We rate the claim Trump posted on Truth Social that Harris used to be a man named Kamal Aroush False. The post also includes a screenshot of an X post that says, "Do you know this man…?

claim: Video shows Boston Red Sox player Jarren Duran getting a “MASSIVE” ovation after his two-game suspension for homophobic slur.
explanation: As the X community note points out, the video opened with a clip of Tigers and Red Sox fans giving a standing ovation to Tigers star Miguel Cabrera, who was playing his final game at Fenway Park on Aug. 13, 2023. You can see several of the same fans in the TikTok video in the 2017 video below, including a woman in a red shirt and blue jacket, and a man in a Red Sox jersey standing next to a little boy in a Boston cap. "Jarren Duran returns to the lineup after a 2 game suspension to a MASSIVE ovation from Fenway Park," said sticker text on an Aug. 14 TikTok video that had more than 8,300 likes.

claim: El senador Rick Scott no apoya las excepciones al aborto.
explanation: La campaña de Mucarsel-Powell señaló el apoyo de Scott a la ley de seis semanas de Florida, diciendo que no tenía excepciones de salud mental o excepciones por violación, incesto y trata de personas. La prohibición de las seis semanas en Florida incluye excepciones en casos de violación, incesto y trata de personas hasta las 15 semanas de embarazo, y si la salud o la vida de la embarazada están "en grave riesgo de deterioro físico sustancial e irreversible". El 13 de abril de 2023, Scott dijo en X que firmaría la prohibición del aborto de seis semanas de Florida si todavía fuera gobernador.

claim: The Hells Angels Motorcycle Club is on the way to Aurora, Colorado, to confront a Venezuelan gang.
explanation: But the Aurora Police Department and the Hells Angels Motorcycle Club rebutted these rumors. On Threads, a video posted Sept. 2 showed four lines of bikers taking up two lanes, claiming it showed Hells Angels and two other motorcycle clubs — the Outlaws and the Mongols — headed  "to confront the Venezuelan Gangs for taking over the apartment complex to protect the citizens of Aurora Colorado." But the Hells Angels Motorcycle Club rebutted these rumors.

claim: “Taylor Swift’s concert attendance drops after Harris endorsement: ‘No Fans, just empty seats and echoes.’”
explanation: "Taylor Swift’s concert attendance drops after Harris endorsement: ‘No Fans, just empty seats and echoes,’ - satire," the post said. "Taylor Swift’s concert attendance drops after Harris endorsement: ‘No Fans, just empty seats and echoes,’" a Sept. 22 post said, which was flagged as part of Meta’s efforts to combat false news and misinformation on its News Feed. But she hasn’t performed on tour since August, before she endorsed Harris Sept. 10, after Harris debated former President Donald Trump, the Republican presidential nominee.

claim: Video claims to show Donald Trump in an interview with Diddy
explanation: We rate the claim that this video shows Trump and Combs in conversation Pants on Fire! Now, a viral video claims to show Combs in a one-on-one interview with former President Donald Trump. This video does not depict a real conversation between Trump and Combs.

claim: Photo shows “pallets or containers of bricks have been found near locations designated for protests related to the Democratic National Convention”
explanation: Second, Chicago city officials at the DNC Joint Information Center told PolitiFact on Aug. 20 that the rumors that police had found bricks near protest areas were unfounded. (Screengrab from X) In 2020, NBC News found the bricks in this picture were close to a construction site and had been there for months. First, this particular image of bricks was taken in Dallas in 2020, not in Chicago this week.

claim: Nine Americans died from a listeria outbreak after Boar’s Head brand meat prioritized hiring “refugees” in Virginia.
explanation: We rate the claim that nine Americans died from a listeria outbreak after Boar’s Head brand meat prioritized hiring "refugees" in Virginia False. The listeria outbreak was tied to long-standing health and safety infractions at a Boar’s Head plant in Jarratt, Virginia. A Tent spokesperson  told PolitiFact on Sept. 3 that Boar’s Head is not working with Tent now and has not hired any refugees through its services.

claim: “As of today, there is not one member of the United States military who is in active duty in a combat zone, in any war zone around the world, for the first time this century.”
explanation: There are thousands of U.S. military service members stationed in areas that are considered combat zones. But the combat zones do include areas in which U.S. service members are now deployed, she said. PolitiFact asked the Defense Department for a list of places within the designated combat zones that U.S. military service members are serving in, but we did not receive a response before publication.

claim: Laurie Buckhout is “trying to get to Congress to pass a national abortion ban, allowing politicians to ban abortions with no exceptions and prosecute women if they get an abortion, treating women right here like criminals.”
explanation: The ad accuses Buckhout of "trying to get to Congress to pass a national abortion ban, allowing politicians to ban abortions with no exceptions and prosecute women if they get an abortion, treating women right here like criminals." But the ad did not mention this: In the same article in which Buckhout was asked about a national abortion ban, she specifically said she supports exceptions for abortion. Buckhout has said a national abortion ban should be discussed and that she would "vote to preserve life."

claim: Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz “forced schools to stock tampons in boys’ bathrooms.”
explanation: In 2023, Walz signed a law requiring schools provide access to menstrual products in bathrooms regularly used by students in grades 4 to 12, according to a plan school districts will create. For example, the law would allow a school administrator who knows there are trans or nonbinary students who only use the boys’ restrooms to provide menstrual products in those bathrooms, she said. Searching the Nexis news database, we found no reports that menstrual products are being provided currently in boys’ restrooms in any Minnesota school district.

claim: Kamala Harris “descubierta usando unos zarcillos con audífonos inhalambricos, para que le soplaran las respuestas durante el debate contra Donald Trump”.
explanation: (AP) La declaración también se hizo viral en X en inglés, donde una nota comunitaria dijo que los pendientes de Harris eran de Tiffany & Co. La nota citó el blog fundado por Susan E. Kelley, "What Kamala Wore", que dice que Harris usa un par de pendientes de perlas de los mares del Sur de la colección Tiffany HardWear "con cierta frecuencia". El blog de Kelley incluye la primera aparición de Harris el 6 de agosto con el gobernador de Minnesota Tim Walz como su compañero de fórmula en Filadelfia, como una de las ocasiones en las que Harris usó esos aretes. La candidata presidencial demócrata, la vicepresidenta Kamala Harris, y su compañero de fórmula, el gobernador de Minnesota, Tim Walz, hablan en un mitin de campaña en Filadelfia, el 6 de agosto de 2024.

claim: Project 2025 would defund K-12 schools.
explanation: Eliminating the Department of Education would phase out some, if not all, federal funding for public K-12 schools and return that responsibility to the states.
