For this fact-check, we wanted to know how Project 2025 would affect federal funding for public schools. In an emailed statement, Project 2025 told PolitiFact the fact that school budgets rely on federal money for only a small share of their funding means cutting the department "hardly defunds schools."

claim: “Elon Musk calls for ban on ‘The View,’ ‘I’d rather walk barefoot on hot asphalt than watch ‘The View.’”
explanation: We found no evidence, such as credible news reports or public statements from Musk or "The View," that he is seeking to ban the show from television. Now circulating on social media: purported "breaking" news that "Musk calls for ban on ‘The View’" and said, "I’d rather walk barefoot on hot asphalt than watch ‘The View.’" A July 27 Facebook post sharing the claim was flagged as part of Meta’s efforts to combat false news and misinformation on its News Feed. The blog describes itself as a source of "fake news stories."

claim: Video shows a “strong tornado in Atlanta.”
explanation: A EF2 tornado touched down in Atlanta in April — at night, in the dark — and none of the clips in the Facebook post, all recorded in daylight, show the Georgia twister. We rate claims these clips show a tornado in Atlanta False. The caption of the July 21 Facebook post sharing the video: "Strong tornado in Atlanta USA."

claim: Un video muestra un helicóptero distribuyendo “mosquitos genéticos en Massachusetts, Estados Unidos”.
explanation: Los usuarios en redes sociales que compartieron el video en 2023 lo relacionaron con un programa de Oxitec de mosquitos modificados genéticamente. El Proyecto de Recuperación de Aves del Bosque de Maui, en Hawai, libera mosquitos infectados con Wolbachia en zonas forestales elevadas. "Massachusetts no participa en ninguno de los trabajos de Oxitec, y no tenemos conocimiento de ningún proyecto en el que se liberen mosquitos", dijo Scales.

claim: “Travis Kelce kneels during national anthem fined $10 million and thrown out of the game.”
explanation: "Travis Kelce kneels during national anthem fined $10 million and thrown out of the game," reads text in an image of Kelce kneeling. Kelce has kneeled during the national anthem before. The Aug. 19 post featuring the image said, "Travis Kelce took a knee during the national anthem, a move that cost him a staggering $10 million fine and an immediate ejection from the game."

claim: Says Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene said, “Who else thinks the downfall of America started with Barack Obama?”
explanation: The verified account — "Marjorie Taylor Greene Press Release (Parody)" — posted the message about Obama on Aug. 20. The statement in the Instagram post didn’t appear on that account or Greene’s other verified account, @mtgreenee, as of Sept. 17, and we found no credible news coverage to suggest she posted the statement and then deleted it. Close readers might notice that the name in the X post — "Marjorie Taylor Greene … " — is cut off.

claim: A group of 32 armed Venezuelans took over an apartment building in Chicago.
explanation: The Chicago Police Department did not confirm to PolitiFact whether the specific phone call embedded in the post was real. The Libs of TikTok account reshared the audio posted by the X account Windy City Weather and News, which posts weather information and reports from a Chicago police scanner. Libs of TikTok also shared the post on Instagram.

claim: Lowe’s CEO Marvin Ellison said on CNBC, “If conservatives do not like our values, they should take their money to Home Depot.”
explanation: An Aug. 23 Threads post showed an image of a CNBC logo with this purported quote from Lowe’s CEO Marvin Ellison: "If conservatives do not like our values, they should take their money to Home Depot." (Screenshot from Threads) Ellison didn’t tell CNBC that conservatives should take their money to Home Depot. Social media users shared an image that implied the CEO of Lowe’s urged certain customers to take their business to rival Home Depot.

claim: “In less than 48 hours the United States government is shutting down for good.”
explanation: More than two days after an Instagram post claimed the U.S. government was shuttering forever, American bureaucracy endured. #WWG1WGA," said the caption of a Sept. 2 Instagram post that shared the screenshot, using a hashtag common in the QAnon conspiracy movement. Forty-eight hours after that dire premonition, the U.S. government continued functioning.

claim: “Nike announces termination of contract with Brittney Griner after ‘strong backlash’ from online community.”
explanation: Phoenix Mercury center Brittney Griner signed a deal with Nike in 2013 after she was selected as the No. As of Aug. 26, Nike was selling Griner jerseys on its website. We rate claims Nike announced it’s ending its contract with Griner False.

claim: “Two years ago, Bob Casey promised us his vote will reduce inflation. ... Casey’s vote for reckless spending” made inflation worse.
explanation: The Inflation Reduction Act did not worsen inflation; inflation has fallen by about two-thirds in the two years since the law was signed. So, the Inflation Reduction Act didn’t worsen inflation. The ad distorted the timeline of Casey’s votes and blurred the difference between the Inflation Reduction Act and the American Rescue Plan.

claim: Alexa’s answers to questions about Hurricane Helene prove the storm was “artificially created” or the result of “cloud seeding”
explanation: "Alexa," a woman asked in another Oct. 4 Instagram video, "Did North Carolina use cloud seeding during Hurricane Helene?" Social media posts showed Alexa responding to questions about Hurricane Helene, the Category 4 storm that made landfall in Perry, Florida, Sept. 26, with answers that scientists dispute. "Alexa confirms cloud seeding and hurricane steering!"

claim: North Carolina’s new voting rules in response to Hurricane Helene amount to “cheating” or “stealing.”
explanation: There it is folks… Hurricane Helene was about cheating in the Election🚨 The North Carolina Board of Elections Changed the Voting Rules in the Counties Affected by the Hurricane 10 Days before Early Voting Starts🔴 RULE CHANGES• Easier access to Absentee Ballots• More… pic.twitter.com/uEClhr2H3X The changes amount to a bipartisan effort to help people vote. Posts on X said that North Carolina’s new voting rules in response to Hurricane Helene amount to "cheating" or a plot to "steal" the election. Republican House Speaker Tim Moore told PolitiFact that the election rule changes "will ensure displaced Hurricane Helene victims in the impacted counties can vote, while also providing safeguards such as requiring a bipartisan majority of the county board in order to make significant changes to early voting and initiate out of precinct/out of county voting."

claim: Videos muestran a Kamala Harris ebria.
explanation: El video completo, que incluye declaraciones de Harris a los trabajadores de la campaña de Biden-Harris en Madison, se encuentra abajo. En el video en Facebook del 21 de agosto, Harris habla sobre la democracia mientras suena una música de noticiero de fondo. El video completo de la primera noche de la Convención Nacional Demócrata, como se ve en las imágenes a continuación, muestra a Harris de pie aplaudiendo varias veces.

claim: The plus in LGBTQ+ includes pedophilia.
explanation: Morrow said the plus in LGBTQ+ includes pedophilia. According to a guide compiled by the Human Rights Coalition, the plus sign in LGBTQ+ could include people who are: Contrary to Morrow’s post, Cruz said safety is a primary concern of Equality NC. State superintendent candidate Michele Morrow targeted her Democratic opponent, Mo Green, on social media Monday for accepting an endorsement from Equality North Carolina, a group that champions the LGBTQ+ community, which includes people who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or queer.

claim: Says U.S. Sen. Tammy Baldwin "believes taxpayer dollars should be used for abortion."
explanation: You have someone like Tammy Baldwin that believes taxpayer dollars should be used for abortion. Steil claimed Baldwin "believes taxpayer dollars should be used for abortion." When we asked Steil’s office for evidence, his staff noted that Baldwin voted against the No Taxpayer Funding for Abortion and Abortion Insurance Full Disclosure Act in January 2019.

claim: “JD Vance actually sent a letter last year to the Department of Justice saying, ‘enforce the Comstock Act.’”
explanation: In January 2023, Vance joined about 40 congressional Republicans in sending a letter urging the U.S. Justice Department to enforce the Comstock Act to crack down on mailing abortion pills, which are used in the majority of U.S. abortions. Warren said Vance sent a letter to the Justice Department asking it to enforce the Comstock Act. The letter Vance signed was in response to the release of a Justice Department memo saying U.S. law doesn’t prohibit the mailing of abortion medication as long as the sender doesn’t intend for the medication to be used illegally.

claim: Photos show a toddler “saved” by Deputy Tyler Cooper.
explanation: Yet another post shared Sept. 16 in a group for residents of Parlier, California, and four other California cities, including Fresno, to buy, sell and trade goods said the boy was found "walking behind a home here in Parlier." "This little boy approximately 2 years old was found last night walking behind a home here in #San Diego," read a Sept. 15 post shared in a public Facebook group called "Entrepreneurs San Diego." The only thing different in this post was where the boy was supposedly found: "walking behind a home here in #Oxnard."

claim: CDC warns a third of adults may die from dangerous bacteria in ramen noodles.
explanation: The claim that the CDC warned that people are at risk of death from a deadly bacteria found in ramen noodles is not backed by evidence. We searched the FDA’s recalls, market withdrawals and safety alerts website and found nothing about ramen noodle products being recalled because of a deadly bacteria. "A deadly outbreak linked to ramen noodles has sparked global fear as multiple deaths have been reported," a Sept. 17 Instagram video said through a talking fish.

claim: Photo shows former President Donald Trump “asleep at the 2017 NATO summit.”
explanation: We rate claims this photo shows Trump sleeping at the 2017 NATO summit False. "Remember that time when Trump fell asleep at the 2017 NATO summit? An old photo of former President Donald Trump, sitting with his head bowed, is being shared anew on social media and presented as evidence that he was caught sleeping at a 2017 NATO summit in Brussels, Belgium.

claim: Maxine Waters told her followers on X not to follow Omar Navarro because he is a “Hispanic Republican.”
explanation: We rate the claim that Maxine Waters told her followers on X not to follow Omar Navarro because he is a Hispanic Republican Pants on Fire! He’s a young Hispanic Republican spreading lies on Instagram," a screenshot on Instagram purporting to be from Waters’ official social media account says. But Waters did not make an online post to discourage people from following Navarro, as social media users claimed.

claim: Rep. Elissa Slotkin’s vote for the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act was a vote to “cut Medicare benefits for seniors.”
explanation: Mutual of Omaha said in March that it will exit the Medicare Prescription Drug Plan market at year’s end because of the "pending impact of the Inflation Reduction Act" on Medicare drug plans. Medicare Part D, which offers insurance coverage for prescriptions, is a voluntary program, and about 50 million of the 65 million people Medicare covers are enrolled — either through a standalone Prescription Drug Plan or through Medicare Advantage. The column argued that funding changes under the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act to Medicare Part D — which helps cover prescription drug costs — could lead to higher premiums and fewer benefits for older Americans.

claim: Video shows a CNN segment about “veterans cancelling their auto insurance.”
explanation: The video in the Aug. 18 Facebook post features CNN’s logo and a "breaking news" chyron that says: "Veterans are cancelling their auto insurance and doing this instead." What looks like a CNN breaking news segment about car insurance for veterans is drawing attention on social media, but maybe not the attention the account posting the video hoped for. "As a veteran, I qualified for the 2024 Veteran & Military Monetary Relief Plan AND apparently you can use it to cut down on your auto insurance," the post said.

claim: Image of people boarding up a window shows Michigan election officials are “preparing to steal this election”
explanation: We rate the claim that this image shows windows being boarded up in Michigan vote counting centers False. The claim showed up on our radar Sept. 24, when a Michigan attorney shared an image on X of a man boarding up windows with plywood. (Screenshot of X post) But Michigan isn’t boarding up its election centers with weeks until Election Day.

claim: Photo shows Israeli swimmers protesting Olympic rules by spelling out “bring them home.”
explanation: The Israeli artistic swimming team also shared the image on Instagram that day. We rate claims this photo shows Israel’s national swimming team protesting Olympic rules False. Spiegel, who also didn’t respond to PolitiFact’s questions about the post, told Agence France-Presse that it was "a fake news story."

claim: Video shows helicopter “dropping millions” of mosquitoes in Massachusetts towns hit by eastern equine encephalitis virus.
explanation: An Aug. 25 Instagram post tied the virus’s outbreak to a video it claimed showed a helicopter dropping mosquitoes from the sky. An Instagram post claimed millions of mosquitoes released from a helicopter could be tied to an outbreak of eastern equine encephalitis, a deadly mosquito-borne virus. A TikTok video from 2023 shows the same helicopter video seen in the Instagram post.

claim: “Even before the pandemic, America went into a manufacturing recession.”
explanation: There is no official definition for when an industrial sector enters recession, but by two common metrics — employment and output — U.S. manufacturing was tipping negative starting in early 2019, Trump’s third year in office. In other words, manufacturing output was declining for more than a year — then the pandemic hit. Although manufacturing employment rose robustly for the first two years of Trump’s term, this job growth stalled in his third year and fell slightly before the pandemic hit during his fourth year.

claim: Photo of Kamala Harris’ Aug. 7 rally near Detroit was AI-generated and “there was nobody there.” Attendees pictured “didn’t exist.”
explanation: Supporters listen Aug. 7, 2024, as Democratic presidential nominee Vice President Kamala Harris speaks at a campaign rally in Romulus, Michigan. "This is an actual photo of a 15,000-person crowd for Harris-Walz in Michigan," the Harris campaign wrote in an Aug. 11 X post, sharing the contested photo. Lavora Barnes, Michigan’s Democratic Party chair, shared a photo on X of herself addressing the Aug. 7 crowd and joked about Trump’s AI-generated crowd claim.

claim: “Un grupo de 32 venezolanos armados tomaron esta noche un edificio de apartamentos en Chicago”.
explanation: La publicación contiene un audio en el que un operador de la policía detalla el informe de una persona que llama. Calificamos la declaración de que un grupo de 32 venezolanos armados tomaron un edificio de apartamentos en Chicago como Falsa. El departamento dijo que alguien hizo una llamada de servicio sobre venezolanos armados que estaban entrando ilegalmente a la propiedad, pero que el incidente reportado en la llamada "no fue de buena fe" o "no fue real".

claim: Video shows “Kamala Harris describing how she can ruin lives with the 'swipe of a pen.’"
explanation: We rate the claim that this video shows Harris describing ruining lives with her pen False. But a viral video appears to show her speaking boastfully about how she could ruin lives as a prosecutor. "Power hungry Kamala Harris describing how she can ruin lives with the 'swipe of a pen,’" an Aug. 16 X post said.

claim: "El gran respaldo de Taylor Swift" a Kamala Harris "le cuesta $125 millones en acuerdos de marca".
explanation: Al hacer una búsqueda en Google del titular de la publicación traducido al inglés, encontramos un artículo publicado el 12 de septiembre con una imagen de Harris y Swift en Esspots, una página web que se describe como creadora de contenido satírico. Pero PolitiFact no encontró noticias verídicas en la base de datos Nexis o declaraciones públicas de Swift diciendo que perdió millones de dólares en acuerdos con marcas por apoyar a Harris. No sabemos si el acuerdo con CoverGirl del 2010 sigue vigente, pero tampoco encontramos comunicados de prensa o publicaciones en las redes sociales de  la empresa de cosméticos, que pertenece a la empresa Coty, que digan que  terminó alguna relación con Swift debido al respaldo a Harris.

claim: “The last union member on a national ticket (was) Ronald Reagan.”
explanation: Walz said that, before himself, "the last union member on a national ticket (was) Ronald Reagan." He repeated this claim more recently, in a Sept. 21 appearance in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, when he said that "the last union member on a national ticket (was) Ronald Reagan." There’s one problem with the talking point: A card-carrying union member named Donald Trump was on the ballot more recently, in both 2016 and 2020.

claim: A video shows a body that Israel embedded with a bomb exploding during a Palestinian funeral procession.
explanation: We rate the claim that a video shows a body that Israel embedded with a bomb exploding during a Palestinian funeral procession False. A graphic video shows an explosion at a funeral procession. But the video does not show a recent Palestinian funeral.

claim: Vice President Kamala Harris was fired from McDonald’s for stealing.
explanation: In the comments of its McDonald’s post, America’s Last Line of Defense linked to an article by Dunning-Kruger Times that cited a McDonald’s spokesperson who said Harris was fired for stealing "‘a substantial amount’ of chicken McNuggets." We rate the claim that Harris was fired from McDonald’s for stealing Pants on Fire! Her campaign told PolitiFact that Harris worked at a McDonald’s in Alameda, California, in the summer of 1983.

claim: "La nueva ley de condonación elimina $15,000 de la deuda de tarjetas de crédito para todos los estadounidenses".
explanation: "La nueva ley de condonación elimina $15,000 de la deuda de tarjetas de crédito para todos los estadounidenses", dice una publicación en Facebook del 3 de septiembre. La Oficina para la Protección Financiera del Consumidor (CFPB, por sus siglas en inglés), recomienda a los consumidores a contratar a un asesor de crédito sin fines de lucro y negociar directamente con la compañía de tarjetas de crédito, antes de contratar a una compañía de alivio de deudas. No existe una "nueva ley de condonación" de deudas de tarjetas de crédito, calificamos la publicación como Falsa.

claim: “Communicable diseases like HIV and TB (tuberculosis) have skyrocketed” after Haitian migrants came to Springfield, Ohio.
explanation: The complete source of the TB data — Clark County’s Communicable Disease Cumulative Report 2013 to 2023 — showed four TB cases in 2023, an increase of one case over the previous year. Official HIV case data also shows a rise in one case from 2021 to 2022, and preliminary data shows there were 29 HIV cases in 2023. A Trump-Vance campaign spokesperson sent us data screenshots showing Clark County HIV and TB case rates from 2013 to 2023.

claim: In South Philadelphia, people are “getting paid $700 a week to go to wherever Kamala’s campaign tells them to go to.”
explanation: Are people getting paid to attend Vice President Kamala Harris’ campaign events? We rate the claim that people are "getting paid $700 a week"  to go to Harris’ campaign events False. The claim that people are getting paid to attend events is not new.

claim: "Dallas County Texas (tells) election workers to (illegally) lie on registration & use a church address to register homeless people to vote!”
explanation: It said state law is clear that you don’t need a home to vote, and that voters can use an address other than their residential address as a mailing address. An X post said that Dallas County election workers were telling trainees to illegally lie on voter applications and use a church address to register voters. "State law is very clear: having a home is not a requirement to be eligible to register to vote, and voters can use an address other than their residential address as a mailing address."

claim: Dr. Leo Ferreira, a cancer researcher shown in a video clip, was on the plane that crashed in Brazil on Aug. 9.
explanation: A Facebook post claimed that "Dr. Leo Ferreira," a cancer researcher shown in a video clip, was on the plane that crashed Aug. 9 in Brazil. Dr. José Roberto Leonel Ferreira, a professor and radiologist with an imaging center in Brazil, died in the crash, according to news reports. The Associated Press and local news reports said Dr. José Roberto Leonel Ferreira, a recently retired doctor and professor, was among the passengers who died in the crash.

claim: Trump said “you used to be able to get cereal for 20, 30 bucks a pound.”
explanation: We rate the claim that Trump said this viral quote about buying cereal in pounds False. Trump has previously talked about people using an ID for grocery purchases, but he said that in a very different context. That screenshot shows Trump speaking at an Aug. 15 press conference at his golf club in Bedminster, New Jersey.

claim: Florida "put Tom Walz instead of Tim Walz" on its ballots.
explanation: At least three Palm Beach County voters had returned ballots with the misspelling before it was corrected, Link said Sept. 24. The county’s elections supervisor said 257 overseas voters opened an email that contained a link to the ballot with the typo. Any voters concerned about their ballots are welcome to call the Palm Beach County office, Link said.

claim: "Elon Musk anuncia su primera novia (un robot con inteligencia artificial)".
explanation: Tech 4 Peace, un medio de verificación iraquí, signatario de la Red Internacional de Verificación de Hechos, también reportó que la imagen de Musk con la supuesta robot fue creada con inteligencia artificial. La imagen de Musk sentado en un restaurante con una robot humanoide no es real y no hay pruebas de que él anunció "su primera novia (un robot con inteligencia artificial)". El 15 de enero Musk publicó un video en X de uno de los humanoides doblando ropa.

claim: “Elon Musk silences Taylor Swift: Shocking ban wipes out 1 million followers and costs her a staggering $72 million!”
explanation: We rate claims that Musk banned Swift from X False. Singer-songwriter Taylor Swift has more than 95 million followers on X and, as of Sept. 26, her account was active. Still, a Sept. 25 Facebook post claimed that X owner Elon Musk had banished her from the social media site.

claim: “Michael Jordan rejects $400 million Disney offer, stating, ‘I do not collaborate with companies aligned with woke ideologies.’”
explanation: "Breaking: Michael Jordan Rejects $400 Million Disney Offer, Stating ‘I Do Not Collaborate With Companies Aligned With Woke Ideologies’ In Bold Move," an Aug. 3 Facebook post said. Former NBA and "Space Jam" star Michael Jordan didn’t decry The Walt Disney Co., despite a claim bouncing around the internet. In 2023, fact-checkers checked a similar claim that Jordan had turned down a $120 million ad campaign with Disney.

claim: Video shows Vice President Kamala Harris using a teleprompter.
explanation: The post included a video clip without sound that showed Winfrey from behind and Harris in profile as words on a teleprompter scrolled in their foreground. We rate claims this video shows Harris using a teleprompter False. "Apparently Kamala Harris had a freaking TELEPROMPTER during her ‘interview’ with Oprah.

claim: "Samsung drops out of $1 billion advertising campaign with Olympics."
explanation: We rate the claim that Samsung has withdrawn sponsorship for the Olympics False. "The IOC has an agreement with Worldwide Olympic Partner Samsung through 2028," the statement said. Since the opening ceremony, Samsung has continued to share articles about its involvement in the games on its website and social media.

claim: La vicepresidenta Kamala Harris ofrece "solo $750 para los norteamericanos qué perdieron todo con el Huracan" Helene.
explanation: Harris dijo el 2 de octubre en Augusta, Georgia, que FEMA "está proporcionando decenas de miles de dólares más para la gente para ayudarles a ser capaces de hacer frente a la reparación de viviendas, para ser capaz de cubrir un deducible cuando y si tienen seguro, y también los gastos de hotel". La página web de FEMA dijo que esto incluye la financiación de los gastos de reparación de viviendas y alojamiento temporal. La Casa Blanca indicó en una hoja informativa del 2 de octubre que FEMA pagó más de $1 millón a más de 1,400 hogares de Carolina del Norte.

claim: Kamala Harris’ X post said the Olympics’ opening ceremony “made France look great! America, this is what we need to strive towards!”
explanation: A July 28 X post that included a screenshot of what appeared to be a Harris X post that said, "What an impressive show by all of these beautiful and diverse people at the Opening Ceremony of The Olympics! But Harris didn’t post on X with that, or anything else, reacting to the Olympics’ opening ceremony. The fabricated post shows three scenes screenshotted from the July 26 opening ceremony.

claim: "Elon Musk Declares: ‘Pride flags should be banned from classrooms, forever!’"
explanation: The claim that Elon Musk called for pride flags to be banned in classrooms originated on a satire site. Its Sept. 4 post read, "Elon Musk Says: ‘Pride Flags Should Be Banned from Classrooms, Permanently!’ (Satire)" and linked in the comments to the satire site Esspots.com. X owner and Tesla CEO Elon Musk has invited controversy, but a viral claim about him calling for a ban on pride flags started as satire.

claim: Vice President Kamala Harris “even wants to legalize fentanyl.”
explanation: Trump said Harris "wants" to legalize fentanyl as president. Trump said Harris "even wants to legalize fentanyl." Trump said that Harris wants to "legalize" fentanyl, but the ACLU questionnaire asked about "decriminalization."

claim: An image shows the social media profile of the accused suspect in the Apalachee High School shooting.
explanation: We rate claims the image in this post shows the shooting suspect’s X profile False. What appears to be a screenshot of an X profile shows a person wearing what looks like a Harris hat and a shirt that says "trans" with a bio that says: "Kamala 2024 end all MAGAts" and a gun emoji. A Sept. 5 Google search showed that before the shooting even happened, the profile said: "to any lawyers, journos, cops & the CIA: this content is all fake and made up."

claim: The FBI said it would “visit” Elon Musk for writing on X, “No one is even trying to assassinate Biden/Kamala.”
explanation: "Unlike his kids, we’re gonna visit him for this," read the supposed Sept. 16 FBI X post. The post in the purported screenshot didn’t appear on the FBI’s X account as of Sept. 17, and we found no evidence, such as credible news stories, that the agency posted and then deleted the supposed response to Musk. A purported screenshot of the FBI responding to Musk’s post started circulating on social media the next day.

claim: “If you make less than $100,000, Trump is about to raise your taxes. Currently, you’re taxed at 10% and then 12%. He would raise that to a flat rate of 15%.”
explanation: If Trump is elected and he successfully keeps the existing tax brackets in place, people making less than $100,000 will not see their income taxes increase to 15%, because the tax brackets will remain the same as they are today. Still, Trump has never said that he plans to enact the tax policy changes that Project 2025 proposes, so there’s no currently available evidence that he would pursue it. Although the Project 2025 plan doesn’t specifically recommend eliminating the standard deduction, if it were done away with along with most other tax credits, then people making up to $100,000 would end up paying a higher effective tax rate on their whole income, while people on the higher end of the first bracket would be paying lower taxes.

claim: The government gave $3,500 debit cards to immigrants while giving only $750 to Hurricane Helene victims.
explanation: We rate the claim that the government gave $3,500 debit cards to migrants while only giving $750 to Hurricane Helene victims False. The claim about $3,500 debit cards refers to a New York City initiative that began as a pilot program in March and gave prepaid debit cards to 500 migrant families sheltering in New York City hotels to reduce the cost of food distribution. Source: A table emailed to PolitiFact from a spokesperson for New York City Mayor Eric Adams,  showing debit card allotments for migrants based on household size for a 28-day period.

claim: Taylor Swift “admits to having done immoral things with Diddy in the past to gain fame.”
explanation: It led to a blog post that claimed Swift "broke down in tears" during a live interview with Kelce, a tight end for the Kansas City Chiefs NFL team. The blog post gave no further details, such as when and where this purported interview happened. But we found no credible evidence, such as news reporting, public statements or interview footage to corroborate the claim that Swift said she did something "immoral" with Combs.

claim: “FEMA is supposed to help out white people last for the purpose of ‘equity.’ … It’s literally on the FEMA website.”
explanation: But the page doesn’t say that FEMA must help white people last. We rate claims FEMA is supposed to help white people last Pants on Fire! "Under the Biden Harris administration FEMA is supposed to help out white people last for the purpose of ‘equity.’ Don’t believe me?

claim: “Illegal” Haitians in Springfield, Ohio, are “reportedly killing and eating pets.”
explanation: The claim about migrants eating pets is unfounded, with a city spokesperson saying there are no credible reports it’s happening. PolitiFact rated social media posts about the claim False on Sept. 9, and Trump’s debate claim Pants on Fire on Sept. 10. "Kamala Harris and Sherrod Brown are responsible for flooding Springfield, Ohio with thousands of illegal Haitians who are sucking up social services and even reportedly killing and eating pets," Moreno said in the caption of a Sept. 9 Instagram post.

claim: “400,000 workers are now in a union that were not in a union when (Biden) became president.”
explanation: Su said, "Four hundred thousand workers are now in a union that were not in a union when (Biden) became president." During a press conference, she said, "Four hundred thousand workers are now in a union that were not in a union when (Biden) became president." During the last 10 years, union membership was at its highest in 2017 at 14,744,00 — some 300,000 union members more than now.

claim: “Netflix loses 6 million subscribers within hours of donation announcement.”
explanation: "Netflix loses 6 million subscribers within hours of donation announcement: ‘The people have spoken,’" text in an image featuring Harris said in a July 26 Facebook post. We found no evidence to support the claim that Netflix has lost 6 million subscribers as a result of Hasting’s donation. But claims that Netflix lost millions of subscribers as a result originated on a self-described satire page.

claim: Switzerland “no longer recognizes Islam as an official religion.”
explanation: The law followed a 2011 referendum in which Swiss voters approved a proposal to ban face coverings in public. In 2021, the Swiss government opposed the referendum to ban face coverings, as did a coalition of left-leaning parties that called the proposal Islamophobic, The Associated Press reported then. We rate claims Switzerland no longer recognizes Islam False.

claim: Video shows Tim Walz “falsely claims that being gay in Nebraska is ‘illegal’"
explanation: The post included a clip in which Walz said, "Think about this, when I was a kid growing up in Nebraska being gay was illegal, still technically illegal." His full statement: "Think about this, when I was a kid growing up in Nebraska, being gay was illegal, still technically illegal. We rate the claim that Walz "falsely claims that being gay in Nebraska is ‘illegal’" False.

claim: “Kamala involved in P-Diddy’s rapes and assaults.”
explanation: We searched Google and the Nexis news database and found no credible reports of Harris being involved in Combs’ alleged crimes. Harris was California’s attorney general from 2011 to 2017. The Instagram video presented no evidence to support the claim, citing only Harris’ role as California’s attorney general during the period in which Combs supposedly committed the crimes.

claim: FEMA “blocked a runway” at a South Carolina airport and “halted” hurricane relief flights.
explanation: An Instagram video said that FEMA closed a runway at a Greenville, South Carolina, airport and halted flights of donated supplies to hurricane victims. Roberts said in the video that FEMA was at the airport only for medical reasons and the group has had no contact with the federal agency. An airport spokesperson said a secondary runway was closed for three days for a FEMA contractor, but that closure didn’t affect flights in or out of the airport.

claim: “The entire family of Kamala Harris’ running mate, Tim Walz—they are all supporting Donald Trump.”
explanation: Of course, anyone who watched the Democratic National Convention would know that Walz’s entire family doesn’t support Trump. "Tim Walz’s family back in Nebraska wants you to know something … " he said, sharing the image. Neither did Charles Herbster, a former Nebraska governor candidate who first posted the photo on X.  Herbster, however, didn’t claim Walz’s entire family supported Trump.

claim: “Kamala Harris wants to give $25,000 to illegal aliens to buy American homes.”
explanation: The Vance campaign pointed PolitiFact to Harris’ recently announced proposal that would provide up to $25,000 for first-time homebuyers to put toward a down payment on a home. The Vance campaign argued that migrants could get Social Security numbers that might qualify them for down payment assistance. The Vance campaign said that migrants who entered the U.S. illegally under the Biden-Harris administration could, over time, qualify for Harris’ down payment assistance proposal.

claim: Former President Donald Trump “cut overtime benefits for millions of workers.”
explanation: The Trump administration did not challenge the judge’s ruling and instead set its own overtime rule, which extended overtime pay to millions fewer people than Obama’s rule would have done. In 2016, the Obama administration set a rule that would have raised the salary threshold for overtime pay. The Trump Labor Department’s overtime rule became effective Jan. 1, 2020, and raised the overtime pay eligibility to salaried workers earning $35,568 per year.

claim: Este es “vídeo de una inmigrante haitiana que asesinó y se comió al gato de sus vecinos” en Springfield, Ohio.
explanation: La publicación incluye imágenes de la cámara corporal de un oficial arrestando a una mujer después de que los vecinos dijeran que ella mató y se comió un gato en una zona residencial. Alexis Ferrell, de Canton, Ohio, fue arrestada el 26 de agosto por crueldad animal y alteración del orden público después de que la policía de Canton dijera que torturó, mató y se comió un gato frente a la gente de Canton. Calificamos la declaración de que una inmigrante haitiana asesinó y se comió al gato de sus vecinos en Springfield, Ohio, como Ridícula y Falsa.

claim: "We now have historic low unemployment in America among all groups of people."
explanation: The record low overall unemployment rate is 2.5%, set in 1953. The record low Latino unemployment rate is 3.9%, a level reached once under Trump in 2019 and once under Biden and Harris in 2022. The unemployment rate for these groups currently ranges between six-tenths of a point to 2 percentage points above the record low for that group.

claim: Actor Mel Gibson told talk show host Oprah Winfrey, “You sell children!”
explanation: reads a third quote alongside images of Gibson and Winfrey. reads a quote over what appears to be an image of Gibson generated by artificial intelligence. "You have no proof," reads another quote over a similar image of Winfrey.

claim: Imagen muestra carnet del Partido Comunista de la vicepresidenta Kamala Harris.
explanation: Pero, el Detector que pertenece a la división de noticias de Univision, reportó que la campaña Harris-Walz le dijo que la publicación en redes sociales de un supuesto carnet es falsa. La imagen de un carnet del Partido Comunista con la imagen de Harris fue creada en una página web y no es auténtica. La publicación en Facebook también dice que el carnet fue otorgado personalmente por el segundo secretario del Liga de la Juventud Comunista Leninista de toda la Unión (VLKSM, por sus siglas en ruso) a Harris en 1984.

claim: Video shows buildings crumbling because of an “earthquake in Taiwan.”
explanation: We rate claims that this video shows buildings crumbling because of an earthquake in Taiwan False. The video features dark billowing clouds of debris and buildings crumbling set to an audio track that’s been used in TikTok videos that have been altered to show people, animals and buildings magically materializing in clouds. A recent Facebook post purports to show a series of video clips of the destruction wrought by an "earthquake in Taiwan."

claim: A zero-tolerance policy during the Trump administration "led to less family separation than under Kamala Harris' border policies.”
explanation: The Trump administration zero-tolerance policy meant that U.S. immigration officials separated children and parents who arrived at the border together. They have generally been used to refer to the Trump administration practice of having immigration officials systematically separate children from their parents at the U.S. border to deter illegal border crossings. The terms "family separation" or "child separation" have generally described the Trump administration practice of having immigration officials separate children from their parents at the U.S. border to deter illegal crossings.

claim: Kamala Harris posted about banning Barron Trump’s friend from X because he wore a “Biden Loves Minors” shirt.
explanation: But Vice President Kamala Harris did not demand Loudon’s banning from social media for wearing a "Biden Loves Minors" shirt, as social media users have claimed. We rate the claim that Harris posted about banning Barron Trump’s friend from X because he wore a "Biden Loves Minors" shirt False. Harris has not deleted any posts on her X account in the past 30 days, data collected by Social Blade, a social media analytics website, showed.

claim: “Hurricane Nadine” was on a path to hit Florida on Oct. 10.
explanation: But as of Oct. 12, the administration’s National Hurricane Center had not reported that a storm called Nadine was developing near the U.S. PolitiFact has fact-checked other false claims about a supposed Hurricane Nadine. We rate the claim that a hurricane named Nadine was on a path Oct. 12 to hit Florida False. Other posts on Instagram and Facebook made similar claims about an impending Hurricane Nadine, causing understandable concern after Hurricane Helene hit the state Sept. 26 followed by Hurricane Milton on Oct. 9.

claim: “Melania Trump just filed for divorce MINUTES ago in Palm Beach.”
explanation: We rate the claim that Melania Trump filed for divorce Sept. 1 in Palm Beach Pants on Fire! "The streets are saying Melania Trump just filed for divorce MINUTES ago in Palm Beach," read a Sept. 1 Threads post. On Sept. 1, Jones also posted on X saying, "BREAKING: Melania Trump filed for divorce in Palm Beach* county through online e-file system, time stamped today at 5:12 PM ET."

claim: “Police found human remains and evidence of cannibalism” at Oprah Winfrey’s home.
explanation: More than seven months later, a screenshot of one response is being shared on other social media platforms: "That time police found human remains and evidence of cannibalism in her LA home that she sold in 2013." "why are ppl actually believing this … y’all believe anything"  We rate claims police found evidence of cannibalism and human remains at Winfrey’s home Pants on Fire! We looked for news stories, police reports and other credible sources to corroborate this claim but found none.

claim: Hurricane Helene was the product of intentional weather modification.
explanation: The project focused on a hurricane that struck Florida on Oct. 12, 1947. There’s no proof that Hurricane Helene was formed through weather modification. Allen cited Project Stormfury, a NOAA project in the 1960s that "involved seeding existing hurricanes."

claim: Image shows “Michelle Obama’s necklace from DNC speech” said “Mike.”
explanation: The image in the post is not from the 2024 convention, where she wore navy and had her hair up. "Michelle Obama’s necklace from DNC speech goes instantly viral," read the text that appeared over an image of Obama shared in a Sept. 2 Instagram post. The image in this post was altered.

claim: Says Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz had his stomach pumped “after overingesting horse semen.”
explanation: Although there is a West Point News in West Point, Nebraska, we didn’t find a West Point Daily News. We also found no West Point General Hospital in West Point, Nebraska, or evidence of a Dr. Amanda Thompson who worked there. The photo that appears in the purported stomach-pumping story has been used in connection with his time teaching there at Mankato West High School.

claim: The Minnesota Vikings have denounced Tim Walz: “We don’t suppᴏrt his values.”
explanation: We rate the claim that Minnesota Vikings denounced Walz Pants on Fire! A viral Facebook post claimed the NFL’s Minnesota Vikings distanced itself from home state Gov. "The Minnesota Vikings have denoᴜnced Tim Walz: "We don’t sᴜpport his values," a Sept. 11 Facebook post, featuring a photo of Walz, said.

claim: Karine Jean-Pierre, President Joe Biden’s press secretary, ended a press conference when a reporter asked about Donald Trump’s assassination attempt.
explanation: We rate the claim that Jean-Pierre ended a press conference when a reporter asked about Donald Trump’s second assassination attempt False. News of an apparent second assassination attempt Sept. 15 on former President Donald Trump has led to a slew of misinformation online. In an Instagram reel, Fox News correspondent Peter Doocy says to Jean-Pierre, "It’s been only two days since somebody allegedly tried to kill Donald Trump again, and you’re here at the podium in the White House Briefing Room calling him a ‘threat.’ How many more assassination attempts on Donald Trump until the president and the vice president and you pick a different word to describe Trump other than ‘threat’?"

claim: Shows video of damage from Hurricane Helene.
explanation: We rate the claim that this video shows scenes of Hurricane Helene False. We found a record of the fifth clip showing debris flying across an apartment complex being shared online before Helene. Set to the wail of sirens, a viral video on social media claims to show scenes of Hurricane Helene and its aftermath.

claim: The order of candidate names on North Carolina’s ballot shows a “clear attempt at voter manipulation.”
explanation: There’s no evidence North Carolina’s election ballot has been manipulated. The post said the order of names listed on North Carolina’s ballot shows a "clear attempt at voter manipulation." Pundits and political strategists pay attention to the order of names on a ballot because candidates whose names are listed first tend to perform better than candidates whose names are listed further down the ballot, researchers have found.

claim: Video shows tornadoes in Canada.
explanation: We rate claims this video shows tornadoes in Canada False. "Tornado storm in Canada," the text over the video says. That video was shared as a mirror image of the one seen in the Canada claim.

claim: Vice President Kamala Harris' comments in Augusta, Georgia, show the Biden administration is offering Hurricane Helene victims only $750 in relief.
explanation: We rate the claim that Harris said the Biden administration is providing only $750 to Hurricane Helene victims False. As of Oct. 4, FEMA said the Biden administration provided more than $45 million "in flexible, upfront funding" to Hurricane Helene survivors. The White House said in an Oct. 2 fact sheet that through the Serious Needs Assistance program, FEMA had paid out more than $1 million to more than 1,400 North Carolina households within 24 hours.

claim: "FEMA is out of money and doesn't have money to transfer to those people affected by the hurricane ... they used the money to assist illegal immigrants."
explanation: In a video on X, Hovde claimed FEMA is "out of money" amid Hurricane Helene recovery and the agency "used the money to assist illegal immigrants." FEMA says "no money is being diverted from disaster response needs," such as international or border-related issues. Here’s what FEMA says about claims that Hovde and others have made about Hurricane Helene.

claim: A Republican representative posted a response to the vice presidential debate before it happened.
explanation: We rate claims a genuine Republican congressman prematurely responded to the vice presidential debate False. Did a lawmaker accidentally tweet his partisan analysis of the Oct. 1 vice presidential debate hours before it even began? "Sorry, I had an intern send this out at 7am instead of 7pm," Kimble said in response to the premature debate post.

claim: Kamala Harris’ “plan to tax unrecognized Capital Gains mean(s) if your house goes up in value you will have to pay that Tax Even if you don’t sell your House!”
explanation: Some economists said an unrealized capital gains tax would promote more equity in the tax code. Most crucially: Most Americans wouldn’t have to pay a tax on the appreciated value of their unsold assets and this tax would apply only to people with more than $100 million in wealth. Social media posts claimed Harris’ "plan to tax unrecognized Capital Gains mean(s) if your house goes up in value you will have to pay that Tax Even if you don’t sell your House."

claim: Former President Donald Trump admitted during the Sept. 10 presidential debate that he “blew up the Nord Stream pipeline.”
explanation: An Instagram video said Trump admitted during the Sept. 10 presidential debate that he "blew up the Nord Stream pipeline." Alex Pfeiffer, a Trump campaign team member, also referred PolitiFact to a 2019 Atlantic Council article about Trump imposing sanctions that halted the completion of the Nord Stream 2 pipeline. The Instagram video then cut to Trump at the debate saying, "He said ‘Russia was afraid of him.’ I ended the Nord Stream 2 pipeline."

claim: “Violent crime was up under Donald Trump.”
explanation: But in 2020, the violent crime rate spiked to 385.2 per 100,000 people — higher than any previous year under Trump. Even accounting for the 2020 spike, the violent crime rate in Trump’s final year was still lower than it was during the final year of his predecessor, President Barack Obama. However, the violent crime rate in Trump’s final year was still slightly lower than it was during the final year of his predecessor, Obama.

claim: “Taylor Swift blames Instagram for losing millions of followers after Harris endorsement: ‘It must be a glitch!”
explanation: Swift had more than 283 million Instagram followers when she endorsed Harris. "Taylor Swift blames Instagram for losing millions of followers after Harris endorsement: ‘It must be a glitch!" The number of Taylor Swift’s Instagram followers came under social media scrutiny after she  endorsed Vice President Kamala Harris, the 2024 Democratic presidential nominee Sept. 10.

claim: “The NFL will now use facial recognition at every stadium to verify the identity of everyone at the game.”
explanation: An Instagram post claimed "The NFL will now use facial recognition at every stadium to verify the identity of everyone at the game." "The NFL will now use facial recognition at every stadium to verify the identity of everyone at the game," text added to an image shared Aug. 4 on Instagram read. That mischaracterizes the league’s plan to adopt a new system that will rely on facial authentication software to grant credentialed staff and other stadium workers access to secured areas of the stadium.

claim: Donald Trump “took away protections against discrimination for LGBTQ patients under the Affordable Care Act.”
explanation: Under the Trump administration, the Department of Health and Human Services finalized a rule that removed several LGBTQ+ discrimination protections that the Obama administration had instituted. The Trump administration rolled back numerous Obama-era protections against LGBTQ+ discrimination in health care and insurance coverage under the Affordable Care Act. Although regulations the Trump administration issued undid Obama-era LGBTQ+ discrimination protections in the ACA, a tangled legal landscape means the ability to enforce these anti-discrimination provisions isn’t clear.

claim: U.S. Sen. Sherrod Brown voted to “give illegals taxpayer funded stimulus checks, health care, even Social Security."
explanation: So, an amendment that barred immigrants in the country illegally from receiving benefits would not be in order. Keyes added that Brown again voted June 26, 2013, on an amendment to an immigration bill that prevented immigrants in the country illegally from receiving Social Security for work done illegally. Brown campaign spokesperson Matt Keyes said Brown voted for a similar amendment from then-Sen. Bob Menendez, D-N.J., the same day as the Sessions amendment reaffirming immigrants in the country illegally cannot receive federal benefits.

claim: “Anything that you lose on the tariff from the perspective of the consumer, you gain in higher wages, so you're ultimately much better off.”
explanation: He said some economists say tariffs raise costs for consumers. And higher input costs are also likely to be passed on to consumers, economists said. Our previous review of academic studies of real-world tariffs concluded that consumers ultimately shoulder most of the burden in higher prices for goods, and the burden outweighs tariffs’ economic benefits.

claim: “BREAKING: Police found ‘explosives’ in car near former President Donald Trump’s rally site on Long Island.”
explanation: We rate the claim that police found explosives in a car near Trump’s Uniondale, New York,  rally False. However, local police said that rumors about explosives found near the rally are false. One Instagram user shared a Sept. 18 Daily Mail headline that said, "BREAKING: Police found ‘explosives’ in car near former President Donald Trump’s rally site on Long Island."

claim: “Mike Tyson says he’s willing to box Olympic DUDE with all proceeds to go to a battered women’s charity.”
explanation: "Mike Tyson says he’s willing to box Olympic DUDE with all proceeds to go to a battered women’s charity," an Aug. 2 Threads post said, sharing side-by-side photos of Tyson Khelif. The Boxing Unit, which the International Olympic Committee set up and which handled eligibility for boxing at the 2024 Paris Olympics, affirmed Khelif could compete. But the International Olympic Committee no longer recognizes the International Boxing Association.

claim: “The Montana Secretary of State left Kamala Harris off the ballot.”
explanation: "The Secretary of State notified county election officials that they were troubleshooting missing choices in races in the electronic system for UOCAVA (Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act) voters on Friday morning and were temporarily taking the system offline," Aldrich said. Registered overseas voters are sent physical absentee ballots in the mail 45 days before the election, but also can use the Electronic Absentee System to print a ballot and mail it back or fill in an online ballot, the secretary of state’s website says. Physical absentee ballots for Montana voters who are not overseas will be mailed Oct. 11.

claim: North Carolina removed 747,00 voters from the voter rolls to try to “steal the election.”
explanation: An Instagram post said North Carolina removed 747,00 voters from the voter rolls to try to "steal the election." On Sept. 26, North Carolina said it had removed almost 750,000 ineligible people from its voter rolls since January 2023. Multiple election experts said the removal of about 747,000 registrants from North Carolina’s voter rolls across nearly two years reflects normal list maintenance, which state and federal law requires.

claim: Tim Walz said "we can't afford four more years" of Kamala Harris.
explanation: We rate the claim that Walz said we can’t afford four more years of Harris False. She is the ‘this.’"  It included a video clip of Walz saying, "We can’t afford four more years of this." "In a stunning move, Tim Walz makes the case for Trump: ‘We can't afford four more years of this,’" the conservative podcaster and commentator Benny Johnson posted on X.

claim: “Donald Trump added more to the national debt than any other president, ever.”
explanation: Much of the debt allocated to Trump and Biden will not show up in the federal ledger until years after they leave office. The increase in the federal debt on a president’s watch shows that Trump ranks first for debt in a single term, but Biden is projected to pass him by January 2025, when he leaves office. So far, Biden has added less to the debt — $7.6 trillion — than Trump has.

claim: “Univision accidentally shows that Kamala Harris is reading from a teleprompter live on air.”
explanation: The claim that Harris used a teleprompter in a Univision town hall is not true, the town hall’s monitor and a Univision news president said. Social media users are taking a short video clip from a more than an hourlong Oct. 10 Univision town hall in Las Vegas to falsely claim Vice President Kamala Harris was using a teleprompter. The claim that Harris used a teleprompter mirrors criticism from conservatives that she can’t speak off-script.

claim: The American flag is missing from the Democratic National Convention in Chicago.
explanation: PolitiFact rated False a similar claim that American flags were missing from a 2019 Democratic debate. We rate multiple X posts claiming that the American flag is missing from the 2024 Democratic National Convention in Chicago False. Former President Donald Trump also said there were no American flags at the last in-person DNC in 2016.

claim: Imágenes en este video de un tobogán inflable volando son de la "tormenta tropical helena en Florida EEUU".
explanation: El perfil de Facebook de Cofield dice que él vive en Alabama. El 19 de agosto, la página en Facebook "This is Alabama" que comparte contenido sobre el estado, publicó el video de la tormenta, citando a Cofield como el autor. Encontramos el video compartido en Facebook en esa cuenta de TikTok.

claim: Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz signed a law that would “take children away from their parents if the parents don’t want to consent to sex changes.”
explanation: The law enables Minnesota courts to hear custody cases and issue temporary custody orders in cases in which a parent brings a child to Minnesota to seek gender-affirming care. It amended parts of the Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act to enable Minnesota courts to hear custody cases and issue temporary custody orders in cases in which a parent brings a child to Minnesota to seek gender-affirming care. The law would neither "take away" a parent’s custody rights, nor would it authorize the government to take custody of a child just because a parent objects to gender-affirming care.

claim: An image shows a child affected by recent hurricanes in the United States.
explanation: In the Threads post’s image, the child is wearing a shirt that appears blue or purple. In the other image, the child wears a shirt that appears black. A third image showed the child in yet another boat, in a sleeveless shirt.

claim: “Tim Sheehy told us his health care plan: ‘We need to return health care to pure privatization.’ That would eliminate Medicare.”
explanation: The Tester campaign ad said, "Tim Sheehy told us his health care plan, ‘We need to return health care to pure privatization.’ That would eliminate Medicare." A campaign Facebook ad that began running Sept. 6 said, "Tim Sheehy told us his health care plan: ‘We need to return health care to pure privatization.’ That would eliminate Medicare, increase prescription drug costs, let insurance companies deny coverage for any reason, and force rural hospitals and nursing homes to close. On his campaign website, Sheehy shares criticisms of the U.S. health care system, including the Affordable Care Act, sometimes called "Obamacare."

claim: Of Gaza, “I’ve been there.”
explanation: Trump said he had been to Gaza. Several experts on Israel or Gaza told us that they had no evidence that Trump as president visited Gaza. President Trump has been to Israel."

claim: “Elon Musk backs Caitlin Clark, offers $10 million endorsement.”
explanation: "We post SATIRE, nothing on this page is real," the SpaceX Fanclub Facebook account page says. "Elon Musk backs Caitlin Clark, offers $10 million endorsement: ‘I support you, Caitlin Clark,’" a recent Facebook post said. This claim originated on a self-described satire site and corresponding Facebook account, SpaceX Fanclub.

claim: “100 million ballots (Democrats) prefilled now have the wrong name.”
explanation: (Screenshot from Instagram) Experts told PolitiFact this claim is wrong: There are no official general election ballots yet. "There would be no basis in law for election officials to prepare the ballots for this fall’s general election prior to the deadline for the political parties to identify to those election officials who the party’s nominees are," Edward Foley, Ohio State University law professor, told PolitiFact in a July 26 email. Election law experts say it’s not

claim: Video shows a Ku Klux Klan member at a rally for former President Donald Trump.
explanation: We rate claims that this video shows a KKK member attending a Trump rally False. A Sept. 8 Instagram post sharing the video said: "This video was taken yesterday. In 2023, he shared a video labeled "satire" on the channel that showed him attending another Trump rally with the sign.

claim: “This month alone, more than 16,000 non-citizens have been removed from the voter rolls in 3 states.”
explanation: Greg Abbott said Aug. 26 that the state removed about 1 million ineligible people from the voter rolls since 2021. We don’t know how many of the potential noncitizen voters cast ballots; Texas said 1,930 had a Texas voter history. State election officials routinely take steps to remove ineligible people from the voter rolls in accordance with federal law.

claim: Image shows Hitler in similar scene as Trump.
explanation: We rate the claim that this image shows Hitler in a similar scene as Trump False. Hitler survived assassination attempts but the Threads post’s image of him is altered. The original photo shares no resemblance to the image of Trump on July 13.

claim: Kamala Harris y Tim Walz se tomaron una foto con un cartel comunista.
explanation: Ellos filmaron el video en una oficina de campaña de la vicepresidenta y Walz en el norte de Phoenix, según una cuenta oficial de la campaña de Harris en Arizona. Aunque no encontramos el video editado en estas páginas, los verificadores de Snopes notaron que uno de los creadores de contenido del Dilley Meme Team publicó el 10 de agosto en su cuenta en X el video editado con el nombre "Dilley Meme Team". Al hacer una búsqueda de imagen inversa, PolitiFact encontró que el video original fue publicado el 9 de agosto en X por la cuenta oficial de campaña de Harris.

claim: Video shows Democratic vice presidential candidate Tim Walz dancing to Beyoncé in a cowboy hat and crop top.
explanation: A Sept. 5 Instagram video showed a man who resembled the Democratic vice presidential candidate and Minnesota governor dancing in a red cowboy hat and black leather crop top and pants. "Is it 2024 Democratic Party vice presidential candidate Tim Walz," text on the video read. We rate the claim that a video shows Walz dancing to Beyoncé in a cowboy hat and crop top False.

claim: Proposed Nevada constitutional amendment to protect abortion rights would put “essentially no limit on access to abortion.”
explanation: Brown said Nevada’s proposed constitutional amendment would place "essentially no limit on access to abortion." Brown said the ballot measure would put "essentially no limit on access to abortion." The constitutional amendment would also be harder to repeal than the existing Nevada law, Orentlicher said.

claim: Photo shows Elton John wearing a “MAGA” jacket.
explanation: "Just found out Elton John has publicly supported Trump," a Sept. 7 Threads post sharing the image said. And that goes all the way up to the Supreme Court," John said. "I just thought, ‘Good on you, Donald,’" John said in the video.

claim: “Breaking: WNBA referees disqualify players under league’s new ‘no anthem kneeling’ rule.”
explanation: "BREAKING: WNBA referees disqualify two players under league’s new ‘no anthem kneeling’ rule," an Aug. 22 Facebook post said. The disqualification of two WNBA players for kneeling during the anthem would draw news coverage but we found none. We rate claims that WNBA referees recently disqualified two players over a new anthem rule False.

claim: Eric Hovde “wants to repeal the Affordable Care Act, and kick millions off their health insurance.”
explanation: Baldwin said Hovde "wants to repeal the Affordable Care Act, and kick millions off their health insurance." On the health care page, Hovde doesn’t explicitly say he wants to repeal the Affordable Care Act, rather that the health care system is "deeply flawed and in need of reform." Does Hovde want to repeal the Affordable Care Act, also known as Obamacare?

claim: Photo shows Vice President Kamala Harris “in the 90s.”
explanation: Claudia Jordan, a TV and radio host and a former cast member on Bravo’s "The Real Housewives of Atlanta," shared it in July 2020 on Instagram. "Kamala didn’t look bad in the 90s though," a Sept. 2 Threads post said, sharing an image of three women posing for the camera. An image recently shared on social media isn’t one of them.

claim: Sen. JD Vance is “known for his obsession with couches.”
explanation: Pritzker’s claim referred to the false assertion that Vance wrote in his bestselling 2016 book, "Hillbilly Elegy: A Memoir of a Family and Culture in Crisis," that he had a sexual encounter with a couch. Pritzker’s claim that Vance has an "obsession with couches" is unfounded. NewsGuard, a company that monitors online misinformation, found the claim originated with a satirical X post that said Vance had written about pleasuring himself with a couch.

claim: Tim Walz “changed the Minnesota flag so it could resemble the Somalian flag.”
explanation: He said of the new flag, "We've evolved into a more diverse state and I think it's more reflective of that," according to a May report by WCCO-TV, a CBS News affiliate.. Simon, in a December commission meeting before the final design was chosen, spoke about complaints about the flag design proposals’ resemblance to other countries’ flags; he noted that Iowa’s state flag bears a resemblance to the French flag and Texas’ state flag is similar to Chile’s. But Walz played no role in a state commission’s monthslong process to choose a new design for the state flag and logo, other than appointing three commission members. Many of those claims were based on proposed Minnesota flag designs and not on the state flag’s final design.

claim: In Wisconsin, “a legislative committee cannot release funding.”
explanation: James claimed that a legislative committee cannot release funding, but his staff later said he misspoke, and meant that the Joint Finance Committee of the Legislature cannot release the PFAS trust fund because Evers has already vetoed it. Democrats say that the Joint Finance Committee could release the funding and allow the Department of Natural Resources to spend it. Evers has already vetoed the legislation meant to guide how the PFAS money is spent, meaning that if the committee were to release the funding anyway, it could cause problems.

claim: Photo from an Aug. 14 campaign event in Michigan shows “JD Vance couldn’t fill a small room.”
explanation: Kamala’s Wins shared the photo at 12:13 p.m. About an hour later, at 1:30 p.m., Meryl Kornfield, a staff writer at The Washington Post, posted on X a photo from the Vance campaign event that showed a bigger crowd with almost every seat occupied. An X account called Kamala’s Wins shared a photo Aug. 14 from Vance’s rally that day outside Cordes Inc., a Byron Center, Michigan, trucking company. "The photo of a virtually empty Vance rally going around doesn’t accurately depict the crowd size now.

claim: “Hollywood actor Kurt Russell just said: ‘It is now proven, beyond a shadow of a doubt that Kamala Harris and Joe Biden CHEATED in the 2020 election with mail-in ballots.’”
explanation: Former Arizona congressional candidate Josh Barnett shared a post on Instagram that attributed a quote to Russell claiming "beyond a shadow of a doubt" that President Joe Biden’s 2020 election win was fraudulent. We rate the claim that Russell said Harris and Biden "cheated" in the 2020 election False. The post, which is a screenshot of a post on X, read: "Hollywood Actor Kurt Russell just said: ‘It is now proven, beyond a shadow of a doubt that Kamala Harris and Joe Biden CHEATED in the 2020 election with mail-in ballots.’" Barnett captioned the post, "Fact check: TRUE."

claim: Patron, Don Julio and Pink Whitney tequila recalled because they contained fecal matter.
explanation: A Facebook post’s claim that Patron, Don Julio and Pink Whitney tequila products were recalled due to containing fecal matter lacks evidence. We checked the websites and social media accounts for Patron, Don Julio and Pink Whitney and found nothing about a product recall. We found multiple social media posts making the same claim on Facebook, Threads, TikTok and X.

claim: Photo shows Kamala Harris posing beside Sean “Diddy” Combs.
explanation: A Sept. 17 Facebook post shared a screenshot of an X post with this photo, which appears to show Harris at an event with Combs and another woman. But the 2001 photo doesn’t show Harris and Combs posing together. A photo circulating online claims to show a young Kamala Harris posing beside music magnate Sean "Diddy" Combs, who faces federal sex trafficking charges.

claim: “Taylor Swift’s concert tickets” fell to $75 after she endorsed Kamala Harris
explanation: The claim that Swift’s concert ticket prices suddenly dropped to $75 following her endorsement of Harris is also rated False. "Taylor Swift’s concert ticket prices went from being worth thousands to just over $75 since her ‘big endorsement’" read an Oct. 4 Facebook post. Tickets for Taylor Swift’s remaining tour dates in the U.S. and Canada are sold out, and tickets on resale markets such as StubHub, SeatGeek, and Vivid Seats are mostly priced at more than $1,000 each .

claim: Elon Musk said, “Anyone caught promoting propaganda will be suspended from X.”
explanation: We rate claims Musk threatened to suspend accounts promoting propaganda False. The X post doesn’t appear on Musk’s account, and searching more broadly for the statement we found no credible news coverage that mentioned it or public statements from Musk expressing such a sentiment. A purported screenshot of such an X post from Musk has nevertheless been spreading on social media, including in a Sept. 7 Threads post.

claim: "Maduro llega a Rusia para pedir ayuda armamentista ante las relaciones negativas con los países americanos".
explanation: Según nuestra búsqueda de noticias, la última vez que Maduro estuvo en Rusia de visita oficial fue en septiembre de 2019. Una búsqueda de la palabra "Rusia" en la página web de prensa de Maduro no dió resultados diciendo que Maduro fue a Rusia este año. Al hacer una búsqueda de imagen inversa en Google, encontramos el video en X, publicado por la cuenta del Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Comunicación e Información de Venezuela el 4 de diciembre de 2018.

claim: “Elon Musk pide la prohibición de ‘The View’, ‘prefiero caminar descalzo sobre asfalto caliente que ver The View’”.
explanation: No encontramos pruebas, como noticias verídicas o declaraciones públicas de Musk o de "The View", de que Musk esté intentando prohibir el programa de televisión. ¿Qué tiene más audiencia, el programa de debate "The View" de la cadena ABC o la información falsa de que el empresario Elon Musk quiere terminar el programa? "Elon Musk pide la prohibición de ‘The View’, ‘prefiero caminar descalzo sobre el asfalto caliente que ver ‘The View’", dice una publicación en Facebook del 21 de agosto.

claim: Image claims Tiger Woods said “Kamala's fake black accent is embarrassing and extremely offensive.”
explanation: But Woods didn’t say this. Now, an Instagram post says Woods publicly criticized Vice President Kamala Harris, whose father is Jamaican and whose mother was Indian, as not being authentically Black. We rate the claim that Woods criticized Harris’ accent Pants on Fire!

claim: Melania Trump “was an escort.”
explanation: Images of nude art including Michelangelo’s famous "David" sculpture appear in the video as Trump speaks. Nearly a decade later, there is no more evidence to back up the claim that Melania Trump was an escort. In August 2016, the Daily Mail published an article about Trump’s nude modeling work and included allegations that she had worked as an escort.

claim: “Breaking: Kansas City Chiefs refuse to host a Pride Night, ‘It’s woke agenda’”
explanation: We rate the claim that the Kansas City Chiefs refused to host a Pride Night False. "Breaking: Kansas City Chiefs refuse to host a Pride Night, ‘It’s woke ageпda,’" read a viral Oct. 4 Facebook post. That’s because it’s baseless: This claim — and the story the post linked to — originated as satire.

claim: Photos show that Disney World was “destroyed by Hurricane Milton.”
explanation: An Oct. 10 Mouse Trap News article with the headline, "Breaking: Disney World Destroyed By Hurricane Milton," included the same images seen in the Facebook and Instagram posts. "#Breaking News Disney World Destroyed by Hurricane Milton," read the caption on an Oct. 10 Facebook video. There were no legitimate news reports or images released that described the kind of Disney World flooding seen in the Mouse Trap News photos.

claim: Video shows that “JD Vance endorses Project 2025.”
explanation: But the Harris campaign’s claim is inaccurate: This video does not show Vance endorsing Project 2025 — he made these comments in 2021, more than a month before announcing his Senate run and two years before the Project 2025 plan was made public. Vance did not mention nor endorse Project 2025 then. Vance has expressed support from some — but not all — of the ideas Project 2025 promotes.

claim: Video shows Oct. 6, 2024, fires in Beirut caused by Israeli air strikes.
explanation: We rate the claim that a video shows Oct. 6, 2024, fires in Beirut caused by Israeli airstrikes False. "Beirut last night," a user captioned an Oct. 6 Instagram video showing several buildings engulfed in flames. Although the video was AI-generated, authentic footage from CNN, Reuters and The New York Times shows Oct. 6 Israeli air strikes causing fires in Beirut’s southern suburbs.

claim: Image shows a photo of former President Donald Trump wading through floodwater after Hurricane Helene.
explanation: It’s unbelievable that the image in these social media posts would be the only such picture to exist considering that Trump’s presidential campaign draws persistent media attention. Trump’s Georgia trip was widely covered in the media but we found no news reports to corroborate the scene pictured here, much less any other photos or video capturing the moment. Photos and video of Trump in Valdosta published by news outlets including The Associated Press, Getty Images, The Guardian, The New York Times, Fox News, ABC News, CNBC and NBC News show him wearing a navy blue suit, red tie, and a red Make America Great Again hat.

claim: Florida’s six-week abortion law has “no real exceptions. Not for her health. Not even for rape.”
explanation: Florida’s abortion ban does include exceptions for the pregnant woman’s health and life, and for rape and incest up to 15 weeks of pregnancy. Yes on 4’s TV ad said Florida’s six-week abortion law has "no real exceptions. "Assessing how many people who qualify for abortion care under the exceptions are actually able to do so is difficult and the limited health exception leaves out conditions that threaten the health of a pregnant person, but do not pose a risk of substantial and irreversible physical impairment of a major bodily function," Felix said.

claim: “FEMA is closing roads and bridges and causing gridlock traffic during evacuations from Hurricane Milton.”
explanation: As of Oct. 9, the Florida 511 traffic alert system in the Tampa Bay area showed multiple traffic closures on state and U.S. highways, many blocking access to barrier islands and bridges as the storm rolled in. By the morning of Oct. 9, Google maps showed otherwise largely clear highway traffic flow around the Tampa Bay region, as did Florida 511’s traffic map. Starting Oct. 7, Florida suspended tolls, and the Florida Department of Transportation announced vehicles would be allowed to drive on roadway shoulders to help with traffic flow.

claim: Rep. Elissa Slotkin “voted recently to let illegals vote in U.S. elections.”
explanation: It’s already illegal for noncitizens to register and vote under state and federal laws, and a "no" vote on the bill doesn’t change that. "It is already a crime many times over for noncitizens to vote in state and federal elections." Rogers is wrong; Slotkin never voted to allow immigrants in the country illegally to vote in U.S. elections.

claim: El gobernador de Minnesota, Tim Walz, firmó una ley dando educación universitaria gratuita “a los inmigrantes ilegales”.
explanation: El segundo proyecto de ley transfirió $5 millones de ese dinero a un programa diferente de becas de matrícula universitaria para estudiantes que estuvieron en el sistema de hogares de acogida. Walz firmó dos proyectos de ley de educación superior en 2023 y 2024 que cubren los costos de matrícula en las universidades públicas de Minnesota para estudiantes cuyas familias ganan menos de $80,000 al año. Esta es la historia resumida: Walz firmó en ley un programa de becas que cubre la matrícula en las universidades públicas de Minnesota para los estudiantes que cumplan las restricciones de ingresos familiares.

claim: Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp was calling President Joe Biden after Hurricane Helene but "hasn't been able to get him.”
explanation: Trump said Sept. 30 that Kemp had "been calling the president, hasn't been able to get him." Trump did not name the governor who he said couldn’t reach Biden; he could have been referring to Kemp or Democratic North Carolina Gov. He said he talked to Biden on Sept. 29, a day before Trump made the claim.

claim: Candace Owens will host an ABC morning show that will replace “The View.”
explanation: We rate the claim that Candace Owens will host an ABC morning show that will replace "The View" False. ABC has not made an announcement that Owens will be headlining a talk show. "Candace Owens Signs $25 Million Deal With ABC For A Morning Show," a Facebook post says.

claim: Dockworkers went on strike because “they hear screaming children inside shipping containers!”
explanation: We rate claims dockworkers went on strike over children screaming in shipping containers False. We looked for, but found no, credible evidence such as news reporting or public statements from the association to corroborate the claim that its workers went on strike because of hearing children screaming in shipping containers. "SCREAMING CHILDREN INSIDE SHIPPING CONTAINERS," an Oct. 2 post said, sharing a screenshot of a Sept. 30 X post from Real Raw News.

claim: “We’re losing 300,000 people a year to fentanyl that comes through our border. We had it down to the lowest number and now it’s worse than it’s ever been.”
explanation: Moreover, though the number of opioid deaths has risen since Trump left office, it’s incorrect to claim they were the "lowest" while he was president. Annual U.S. fentanyl deaths have increased since he left office, but Trump’s claim about 300,000 deaths has no basis in fact and is contradicted by figures his press secretary shared. Trump’s claim that fentanyl deaths were the "lowest" during his administration and are now worse than ever is also off the mark.

claim: California S.B. 1174 eliminates the requirement for voter ID at polling places.
explanation: Senate Bill 1174 prohibits local governments from requiring voter ID at polling places, but existing state law already says that, in most cases, California voters needn’t show ID before voting at the polls. 1174 prohibits local governments from requiring voter ID at polling places, but existing state law already says that in most cases, California voters don’t need to show ID before voting at the polls. By state law, however, California voters need to show ID to polling place workers only if they are voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a valid form of ID on their registration form, a California secretary of state spokesperson said in an email.

claim: “Mark Robinson skips Board of Education vote on teacher bonuses to hold campaign event.”
explanation: "Mark Robinson skips Board of Education vote on teacher bonuses to hold campaign event," the headline of the press release said. The Stein campaign said Robinson "skips Board of Education vote on teacher bonuses to hold campaign event." And Robinson has attended just over half of State Board of Education meetings, according to data collected by WRAL.

claim: “Arizona was safe” when she moved to the state in 1994, but has become “unsafe.”
explanation: In 2023, the state’s violent crime rate was 409 per 100,000 residents. That’s a 42% decline in violent crime from when Lake first arrived in Arizona. In 1994, Arizona's violent crime rate was 703 per 100,000 residents, according to official FBI data provided by Jeff Asher, co-founder of AH Datalytics, a crime statistics research group.

claim: “The Harris-Biden Administration has been caught fraudulently manipulating Job Statistics.”
