explanation: New Data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics shows that the Administration PADDED THE NUMBERS with an extra 818,000 Jobs that DO NOT EXIST, AND NEVER DID." But the RNC provided no evidence to support Trump’s allegation that the administration had been "caught fraudulently manipulating job statistics." Trump said, "The Harris-Biden Administration has been caught fraudulently manipulating Job Statistics."

claim: Photo shows President Joe Biden lounging on the beach "while towns all over America were being wiped out” by Hurricane Helene.
explanation: The Bidens did visit Rehoboth Beach, Delaware, over the weekend of Sept. 27 to 29, after the hurricane made landfall, but he also issued emergency declarations and spoke to state and local leaders in affected states. Biden told Criswell that he plans to travel to affected communities when it doesn’t disrupt emergency response operations. The White House reported that Biden received several briefs from FEMA throughout the Sept. 27 to 29 weekend on the storm’s ongoing impacts and updates on the emergency response.

claim: C-SPAN captions for a JD Vance speech said, “Single person clapping.”
explanation: LMAO @cspan caption person for the win pic.twitter.com/QHDFYuXplu But C-SPAN aired no such caption, Robin Newton, a spokesperson for the network said. We rate claims that C-SPAN aired the caption "single person clapping" False. a third said.

claim: Rep. Ruben Gallego’s “first act in Congress was to propose legislation to BAN the use of the term ‘illegal alien.’”
explanation: The first bill Gallego proposed in Congress was the Veterans Education Tax Security Act, also known as the VETS Act. Rep. Joaquin Castro, D-Texas — not Gallego — introduced the CHANGE Act on Oct. 21, 2015, with Gallego and 107 other members co-sponsoring it. "Gallego’s first act in Congress was to propose legislation to BAN the use of the term ‘illegal alien,’" Lake wrote.

claim: “Women don't even get their own restroom at the DNC convention.”
explanation: (Screenshot of X post) We saw similar claims that there was "no women’s restroom on site," or that women’s bathrooms were "eliminated" from the convention altogether. A United Center map provided by the DNC shows multiple bathrooms on five of the six floors. A men’s restroom and gender-neutral restroom are near each other, and two women’s restrooms lie a short walk down the hall.

claim: Project 2025 would end gay marriage.
explanation: "The legal recognition of same-sex marriage is not discussed in Project 2025’s Mandate for Leadership," its website says. PolitiFact’s review of Project 2025 found no call to eliminate the right to same-sex marriage. Other posts we saw carried similar doomy messages about gay marriage: Project 2025 will "end marriage equality," "overturn" the right to gay marriage or "ban" gay marriage, they said.

claim: “Sam Brown publicly supported forcing massive cuts to Social Security and Medicare and was caught on tape saying he admires the plan to phase out Social Security and Medicare in five years.”
explanation: Rosen said, "Sam Brown publicly supported forcing massive cuts to Social Security and Medicare and was caught on tape saying he admires the plan to phase out Social Security and Medicare in five years." Sam Brown publicly supported forcing massive cuts to Social Security and Medicare and was caught on tape saying he admires the plan to phase out Social Security and Medicare in five years." Balancing the federal budget is not as simple as it sounds and the balanced budget plan Brown supported would almost guarantee cuts to Social Security and Medicare.

claim: “All students who knelt during the national anthem were rounded up and removed from scholarships” at the University of Texas.
explanation: We rate claims that the University of Texas rounded up student athletes and revoked their scholarships for kneeling during the national anthem False. Rather, an undated blog post with a single paragraph claimed the University of Texas had "recently come under intense scrutiny for reportedly revoking scholarships from five athletes who knelt during the National Anthem to protest racial injustice." "KNEELING: After the University of Texas, all students who knelt during the national anthem were rounded up and REMOVED FROM SCHOLARSHIPS," an Aug. 20 Facebook post said.

claim: "Donald Trump intends to cut Social Security."
explanation: But the Harris campaign ignores most of what Trump has said during the 2024 campaign — namely, that he will not cut Social Security and Medicare. Trump has repeatedly said he would not cut Social Security at campaign rallies in Michigan and Georgia and in multiple posts on his Truth Social platform. "Donald Trump intends to cut Social Security and Medicare," Harris said.

claim: Video shows former President Donald Trump thought he was in North Carolina while he spoke in Pennsylvania.
explanation: Trump suggests he is in North Carolina while he is in Pennsylvania. President Trump was obviously referring to the Front Row Joes from North Carolina in the audience, whom he recognized earlier in his speech." I don’t know, somehow — would that be OK, North Carolina?

claim: McDonald’s “said they have no record whatsoever of Kamala Harris ever working at any of their locations.”
explanation: Harris has mentioned her job at McDonald’s on the campaign trail and in other public appearances. The earliest instance PolitiFact could find of Harris talking about her McDonald’s job is from 2019, when Harris marched with striking McDonald’s workers in Las Vegas. Since launching her 2024 presidential campaign in July, Harris has highlighted her summer job at McDonald’s in campaign ads and on her personal and campaign X accounts.

claim: When New Hampshire gubernatorial nominee Kelly Ayotte served on two companies’ boards, one “laid off 18,000 workers” and the other “laid off 1,200 American workers, moving jobs overseas.”
explanation: Another company for which Ayotte served as a board member, Caterpillar, laid off 1,200 U.S. workers during her tenure, and many of the jobs moved outside the United States. Ayotte served on the board for Blackstone, an investment company that had a joint venture with hospitality company MGM Resorts International, which laid off 18,000 workers in 2020. Ayotte served on the company board of Blackstone, which had a joint venture with MGM Resorts when MGM laid off 18,000 workers as the  COVID-19 pandemic hit and travel slowed dramatically.

claim: Craigslist ad shows “every single person” at Kamala Harris’ Arizona rally was paid.
explanation: We rate the claim that a Craigslist ad shows "every single person" at Kamala Harris’ Arizona rally was paid False. An image of a Craigslist ad then appears with the title, "Actors needed (Phoenix Convention Center)." A Harris-Walz campaign spokesperson told PolitiFact that their "campaign does not pay people to attend rallies, including the recent rally in Arizona," adding that the event was open to the public and people could RSVP until the event reached capacity.

claim: “Kamala Harris permitió la entrada a Estados Unidos de 13.000 extranjeros ilegales condenados por asesinato".
explanation: Pero una sentencia de la Corte Suprema de Estados Unidos, y no la administración de Biden-Harris, dice que no se puede retener indefinidamente a las personas en centros de detención de inmigrantes. Un memorando de 2021 de la administración de Biden ordena a las autoridades de inmigración priorizar la detención de personas que amenacen la seguridad pública. El número de personas en la lista de no detenidos se ha más que duplicado bajo la administración de Biden.

claim: Images show Sean Combs’ booking photos after Sept. 16 arrest.
explanation: As of Sept. 17, no news outlets had yet published a booking photo of Combs following his Sept. 16 arrest, although The Associated Press shared court sketches from his Sept. 17 court appearance and images of Combs’ son leaving a Manhattan federal courthouse. We rate claims these photos were taken after Combs’ Sept. 16 arrest False. "Breaking news," a Sept. 16 Threads post said.

claim: “In Project 2025, you’re going to have to register with a new federal agency when you get pregnant.”
explanation: The Project 2025 document does not call for a new federal agency for pregnancy registration. Walz said that Project 2025 requires women to register with a new federal agency if they get pregnant. Project 2025 would withhold federal money from states that don’t report abortion data to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

claim: Kamala Harris “wants to defund the police.”
explanation: We did not find that Harris called for dissolving police departments. The Harris campaign said that she does not support police defunding (as her campaign told us in 2020) and pointed to statements in which she spoke in favor of police funding. Harris did not go that far — she said police were necessary.

claim: "Typically you have three to four debates in a U.S. Senate race. (Sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis. has) given me one debate, almost a month after early voting has started."
explanation: There’s still a way for voters to cast their ballots — voting absentee by mail — before the Oct. 18 debate. Now, let’s consider the second part of Hovde’s claim: Does the Oct. 18 debate take place "almost a month" after early voting starts in Wisconsin? Early voting is another name for in-person absentee voting, which can take place in Wisconsin from Oct. 22 through Nov. 3.

claim: “Disney World officially moving to Nashville.”
explanation: Text below the headline said: "Breaking news, Disney World is officially moving to Nashville. We rate claims Disney World is moving to Nashville False. We found no credible news stories, press releases or other evidence that Disney World is moving.

claim: “The $750 from FEMA that Kamala Harris is offering them is actually a loan, not real relief. And that if they don’t pay it back the feds can seize their property.”
explanation: On its "Rumor Response" page, FEMA rebutted claims that people who apply for FEMA assistance risk having their property seized or confiscated. These claims are baseless: FEMA’s assistance payment for essential supplies is not a loan, and FEMA does not seize property. "Fact: FEMA disaster assistance are grants which do not need to be repaid."

claim: “Out of the 28 North Carolina counties destroyed by Hurricane Helene, 26 of them supported President Trump in the 2020 election … If you’re wondering why the government hasn’t helped these people, now you know why.”
explanation: Biden didn’t withhold aid to North Carolina counties based on whom their residents supported in the 2020 election. The claim disregards that federal aid was granted to the affected North Carolina counties and omits context about how the government directs aid to disaster-affected areas. Relief and rescue efforts continue in North Carolina after Hurricane Helene, but one person claimed President Joe Biden has not helped the majority of the affected counties because he didn’t win them in 2020.

claim: “Bob Casey and Kamala Harris want to BAN fracking.”
explanation: Harris did support a fracking ban when she ran for president in 2020. Harris said she supported a ban on fracking when she ran for president in 2020. McCormick said Casey and Harris "want to ban fracking."

claim: Elissa Slotkin “gave your hard-earned tax money to illegal immigrants.”
explanation: The bill required a person to have a Social Security number to receive the checks, and most immigrants in the country illegally do not have Social Security numbers. In most cases, people in the country illegally lack Social Security numbers, Lacarte said. The eligibility criteria required people to have Social Security numbers to receive the payments, and the vast majority of people in the country illegally do not have Social Security numbers.

claim: “There’s been a 43% increase in violent crimes since I left office.”
explanation: Both the FBI data and the crime victimization survey are scheduled for release later this year. From 2020 to 2022, a period that largely overlaps with the victimization survey data Trump cited, the FBI data showed violent crime falling by about 4%, rather than rising; it ended up virtually tied with 2019’s prepandemic level. The FBI has released preliminary data for 2023, showing that violent crime dropped by 5.7% from 2022 to 2023.

claim: “Two weeks ago 100 GOP lawmakers voted against additional FEMA funding.”
explanation: A week earlier, a Republican majority voted for their own version of a stopgap funding bill that also included FEMA funding. Reich’s claim is partially accurate because Sept. 25, 18 Senate Republicans and 82 House Republicans voted against a stopgap funding bill to avert a government shutdown. The bill was a much broader funding bill that also included $20 billion for FEMA’s Disaster Relief Fund.

claim: Jacky Rosen “said ending taxes on tips would ‘hurt working Nevada families.’”
explanation: Millionaire Jacky Rosen also said ending taxes on tips would "hurt working Nevada families." Brown said Rosen said a proposal to end federal taxes on tips would "hurt working Nevada families." A Rosen campaign statement included in a June 12 NBC News report described Trump’s promise as "empty talking points," but Rosen also said she supports cutting taxes on tipped workers.

claim: Vice President Kamala Harris’ college professors disparaged her as their “worst student.”
explanation: The Instagram post also claims to quote Harris’ Berkeley law professor, but Harris graduated law school in 1989 at what was then University of California Hastings, now called the University of California College of the Law, San Francisco, or UC Law SF — not Berkeley Law in Berkeley, California. A reverse-image search shows the photo of the man in the Facebook claim is Bradford Grant, Howard University architecture professor. The Facebook post’s language originated Sept. 10 from a satire website, Esspots.com, and was shared on that site’s Facebook account.

claim: El Dr. Juan Rivera lanza "una pastilla revolucionaria" para curar la diabetes.
explanation: La biografía de la página en Facebook que comparte la publicación contiene un enlace a Google Play, la tienda en línea de aplicaciones de Google. La gerente de la práctica del Dr. Rivera confirmó a PolitiFact que la publicación no es verídica. La diabetes es una enfermedad crónica "que afecta la forma en que el cuerpo convierte los alimentos en energía", según la página web de los Centros para el Control y la Prevención de Enfermedades (CDC, por sus siglas en inglés).

claim: Former President Donald Trump posted “0-2” Sept. 15 on Truth Social.
explanation: We rate claims Trump posted "0-2" Sept. 15 on Truth Social False. He posted about the gunman on Truth Social the night of Sept. 15, thanking the Secret Service and other law enforcement officials "for the incredible job done today at Trump International in keeping me, as the 45th President of the United States, and the Republican Nominee in the upcoming Presidential Election, SAFE." An X account called "Donald J. Trump Posts From His Truth Social," which shares Truth Social posts from Trump and his team, featured all of the aforementioned posts when PolitiFact reviewed its feed Sept. 16.

claim: President Joe Biden walked “onto an empty airplane for no reason.”
explanation: We rate claims that Biden boarded an empty plane for no reason False. As fact-checking website Snopes reported, a Black Star Network livestream of Biden and Harris greeting the Americans shows someone on the plane after Biden disembarks again. Biden later boarded the plane that had brought the prisoners to Maryland, setting off a chorus of claims questioning the president’s movements.

claim: “Colin Kaepernick 'screams' as Coach Kyle Shanahan denies his return request: 'The kneeling symbol has no chance of coming back.’”
explanation: "Colin Kaepernick 'SCREAMS' as Coach Kyle Shanahan denies his return request: 'The kneeling symbol has no chance of coming back,’" an Aug. 23 Facebook post said. It’s been seven years since quarterback Colin Kaepernick played for the former San Francisco 49ers — or any NFL team. The post shared an image of Shanahan at a July 29 press conference after a 49ers training camp practice in Santa Clara, California.

claim: Gov. Tim Walz delivered paid family leave in Minnesota but “Republicans are blocking” a Biden-Harris proposal.
explanation: We found that Walz signed paid family leave into law in 2023. "Democrats favor a comprehensive bill that would cover paid family and medical leave for new parents and those needing leave for their own serious illness or to care for a seriously ill family member, while Republicans have focused on leave for new parents only," Waldfogel said. Democrats have proposed paid family leave bills akin to what Walz signed for a decade.

claim: Vice President Kamala Harris “is a communist. … She is really a Marxist.”
explanation: Trump said Harris "is a communist. Asked for evidence to support Trump’s claim that Harris is communist, the Trump campaign singled out her position on price controls. When Trump calls Harris a communist, it evokes fear in Americans who fled authoritarian communist regimes.

claim: Jason Aldean rejected a $500 million music collaboration with Taylor Swift.
explanation: Multiple Facebook users shared an image with text that read, "Jason Aldean Refuses To Let Taylor Swift on Stage, ‘Her Music Is Bubblegum, Not Real Country Artist." We rate the claim that Aldean rejected a $500 million music collaboration with Swift False. The Facebook posts included a caption that said, "Jason Aldean Rejects $500 Million Music Collaboration With Taylor Swift, ‘Her Music Is Woke, No Thanks.’"   These posts were flagged as part of Meta’s efforts to combat false news and misinformation on its News Feed.

claim: "Taylor Swift unexpectedly lost a $125 million brand contract after a massive advertising campaign” endorsing Vice President Kamala Harris.
explanation: But PolitiFact found no credible news stories in the Nexis database or public statements by Swift saying she lost millions of dollars in a brand contract for supporting Harris. "Hot News: Taylor Swift unexpectedly lost a $125 million brand contract after a massive advertising campaign," the post said. The Facebook post’s image of Swift is from a 2020 documentary about the making of her album "Folklore."

claim: Video shows Vice President Kamala Harris “hammered.”
explanation: Let’s break that down." Let’s break that down. The video clip in the Instagram post is about 5 seconds longer than the length of Harris’ actual remarks.

claim: Former President Donald Trump “started out with $400 million on a silver platter and then filed for bankruptcy six times.”
explanation: A comprehensive New York Times review of the Trump family finances in 2018 found that Donald Trump received $413 million from Fred Trump or his estate over the course of his lifetime. When Fred Trump brought Donald Trump into the family business following his college graduation as vice president of multiple subsidiaries, the elder Trump "telegraphed what had become painfully obvious to his family and employees: He did not consider his eldest son, Fred Trump Jr., a viable heir apparent." Fred Trump set up ground leases for two of his developments in Brooklyn, the first of which became active when Donald Trump was 3 years old, the Times reported.

claim: Video muestra policías entrando en una casa en Inglaterra "por comentarios en redes sociales".
explanation: El comunicado incluye un video mostrando varias de las casas a las que entraron, la puerta en una de ellas se parece a la del video en Instagram. Fleur Armitage, una portavoz de la Policía de Gran Manchester, le dijo a PolitiFact que el video en Instagram no muestra lo que la publicación dice. El 29 de julio en la ciudad de Southport, en el noroeste de Inglaterra, tres niñas fueron apuñaladas mortalmente y cinco menores y dos adultos fueron heridos gravemente en un centro comunitario, según la policía local.

claim: En el sur de Filadelfia, la campaña de Kamala Harris “está pagando a la gente $700 por semana para viajar y asistir a todos sus eventos”.
explanation: "Acabo de salir de mi salón de manicura y mi técnico de uñas... dijo que su primo está en el sur de Filadelfia y escuchen esto, le pagan $700 por semana para ir a donde la campaña de Kamala les diga que vayan", dijo la mujer en inglés en la publicación del 21 de septiembre. Reuters también calificó como falsa una afirmación que sugería que los autobuses de la campaña de Harris se utilizaron para llevar a las personas a un evento de campaña el 12 de septiembre en Charlotte, Carolina del Norte. El clip muestra a una mujer contando una historia en inglés sobre cómo la campaña de Harris supuestamente le paga a la prima de su manicurista para que asista a los eventos de campaña de la candidata presidencial demócrata.

claim: “Caitlin Clark declines $1 million offer from ABC to appear on ‘The View.’”
explanation: "BREAKING: Caitlin Clark declines $1 million offer from ABC to appear on ‘The View,’" an Aug. 5 Facebook post said. We rate claims Clark turned down a $1 million "The View" appearance False. The Facebook post resharing the claim did not label it as satire.

claim: “Less than three months ago, Kamala Harris and her administration blocked 300,000 unvetted Haitian migrants from being deported out of our country."
explanation: Trump Jr. is inaccurate that the Haitians granted Temporary Protected Status are "unvetted." But the Temporary Protected Status program is also available to people who don’t have deportation orders. Trump Jr.'s claim that Temporary Protected Status recipients are unvetted is inaccurate.

claim: Democrats dyed the “Chicago River red to celebrate abortion.”
explanation: "DNC has dyed Chicago River red to celebrate abortion." "The #DNC2024CHICAGO dyed the river red to celebrate abortion." Yet another claimed that the city of Chicago had dyed the river to celebrate abortion.

claim: Immigrants get $2,000 each time they cross the border illegally.
explanation: The federal government does not give migrants $2,000 every time they cross the border illegally, despite claims made by Joe Rogan on his podcast. We rate the claim that immigrants get $2,000 each time they cross the border illegally False. People who cross the border illegally a second time can also be fined and imprisoned for up to two years.

claim: Bill Gates dijo que "estamos tomando cosas que son ya sabes organismos genéticamente modificados y los estamos inyectando en los brazos de niños pequeños" en el contexto de las vacunas.
explanation: "Estamos tomando cosas que son ya sabes organismos genéticamente modificados y los estamos inyectando en los brazos de niños pequeños y los inyectamos directamente en la vena", dice Gates en la publicación del 20 de septiembre. Bill Gates aludió a la necesidad de realizar pruebas de seguridad a los alimentos con organismos genéticamente modificados, semejante a las pruebas que se hacen con los medicamentos. Este video también mostraba a Gates diciendo que inyectaban a los niños con organismos modificados, sin explicar que él estaba aludiendo a la necesidad de realizar más pruebas a los alimentos genéticamente modificados.

claim: "Mike Pence endorsed Kamala Harris.”
explanation: We found no evidence that Pence has publicly endorsed Harris for president and a spokesperson for an organization Pence founded said he doesn’t plan to endorse her. Pence has said he will not endorse Trump for president. But some social media posts are claiming that Pence has endorsed Vice President Kamala Harris, the presumptive Democratic nominee for president.

claim: Video shows “people attempting to flee Florida & Hurricane Milton.”
explanation: "People attempting to flee Florida & Hurricane Milton," an Oct. 9 Threads post sharing the video said. We rate claims that a video shows people stuck on bridges during Hurricane Milton False. "Heavy traffic jam due to waterlogging in Mumbai," another Sept. 25 Instagram post said.

claim: The “‘Inflation Reduction Act’ increased inflation and drove prices sky high!”
explanation: A Sheehy post said the Inflation Reduction Act that Tester supported "increased inflation and drove prices sky high!" It doesn’t mean that the Inflation Reduction Act caused inflation to ease. Tester voted for the Inflation Reduction Act in August 2022.

claim: Rep. Ruben Gallego is “controlled by the cartels. His own father was a Colombian drug trafficker, and so he’s got links to the cartel.”
explanation: But Gallego’s father has been largely absent from Gallego’s life since Gallego was in junior high school and his parents divorced. Gallego wrote that his father was almost entirely absent from his life after the divorce, making Lake’s accusation that Gallego has "links to the cartel" through his father dubious. Speaking Sept. 27 with Newsmax host Greg Kelly, Lake theorized a connection between Gallego and drug cartels because his father was arrested for drug crimes when Gallego was a child.

claim: “Serena Williams reportedly passes away following tragic car crash in Texas.”
explanation: "‘FAREWELL TO A TENNIS LEGENDS’: Serena Williams reportedly passes away following tragic car crash in Texas. The posts featured images of Williams and an aerial shot of a crash scene. Details surrounding the crash remain scarce, but early reports indicate that Williams was involved in a severe accident that occurred earlier this morning.

claim: Former President Donald Trump "intends to enact what, in effect, is a national sales tax ... that would raise prices on middle-class families by almost $4,000 a year."
explanation: Harris said Trump "intends to enact what, in effect, is a national sales tax — call it a Trump tax — that would raise prices on middle-class families by almost $4,000 a year." Even as Trump proposes tax cuts that would benefit wealthier Americans, Harris said, he "intends to enact what, in effect, is a national sales tax — call it a Trump tax — that would raise prices on middle-class families by almost $4,000 a year." Trump has proposed a 10% tariff (and at least once said up to 20%) on all nondomestic goods sold in the U.S., along with a 60% tariff on Chinese goods.

claim: Videos of media talking about Tim Walz as a "happy warrior" are proof of government propaganda legalized by Barack Obama.
explanation: An Instagram post said videos of media talking about Walz as a "happy warrior" are proof of government propaganda legalized by Barack Obama. The Instagram post’s narrator referred to a law change during Obama’s administration that she said "legalized government propaganda" and led to the news outlets "repeating the same Democratic talking points." False social media posts in recent years have said the law legalized government propaganda in the U.S.

claim: Florida’s Amendment 3 is “the monopoly amendment.”
explanation: Large medical marijuana companies in Florida back the ballot measure to legalize marijuana for recreational use and one in particular, Trulieve, has contributed about $93 million to help the amendment pass. Florida has 25 licensed medical marijuana companies, referred to by law as "medical marijuana treatment centers." The measure says medical marijuana treatment centers, or other state licensed entities, will be able to sell recreational marijuana products without criminal or civil liability.
